docs.title: 1. Install OADP Operator
docs.text: ./scripts/01-install-oadp.sh

docs.title: 2. Configure S3 Storage
docs.text: Choose one of the following options:

docs.title: Option A: ODF RGW (Recommended for homelab)
docs.text:
Uses ODF's built-in Ceph RGW for S3-compatible storage. No external storage required.

# Create bucket and credentials in one step
./scripts/setup-rgw-credentials.sh

# Deploy DataProtectionApplication
./scripts/deploy-dpa-rgw.sh

docs.title: Option B: External S3 (AWS, MinIO, etc.)
docs.text:
Edit the credentials template:

cp manifests/04-credentials-secret.yaml.template manifests/04-credentials-secret.yaml
# Edit with your S3 credentials
oc apply -f manifests/04-credentials-secret.yaml

Deploy DPA:

export S3_BUCKET="hcp-backups"
export S3_ENDPOINT="https://s3.example.com"
export S3_REGION="us-east-1"

envsubst < manifests/05-dpa.yaml.template | oc apply -f -

docs.title: 4. Perform Backup
docs.text: ./scripts/02-backup-control-plane.sh <hosted-cluster-name> <namespace>

docs.title: 5. Restore (if needed)
docs.text:
# Same management cluster
./scripts/04-restore-same-cluster.sh <backup-name>

# New management cluster
./scripts/05-restore-new-cluster.sh <backup-name>

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• OADP Operator installed on management cluster
  • S3-compatible storage:
  • ODF RGW (recommended) - Built-in Ceph object storage, no external deps
  • ODF MCG (NooBaa)
  • MinIO
  • AWS S3
  • oc CLI with cluster-admin access
  • velero CLI (optional, for detailed status)

docs.title: What Gets Backed Up
docs.text: Component Description HostedCluster CR Cluster configuration HostedControlPlane CR Control plane settings NodePool CRs Worker node configuration Secrets Cluster secrets (pull-secret, SSH keys, etc.) ConfigMaps Configuration data etcd data Cluster state (via volume snapshots) ServiceAccounts RBAC identities Roles/RoleBindings RBAC permissions

docs.title: Restore Scenarios
docs.text:
1. Same Management Cluster - Recover from data corruption
  2. New Management Cluster - Migrate or recover from total failure

docs.title: Important Notes
docs.text:
• Data plane workloads continue running during management cluster issues
  • External DNS is required for cross-cluster restore
  • Always verify backups with ./scripts/verify-backup.sh

docs.title: OADP HCP Backup Setup - Step by Step
docs.text: Date: 2026-01-19 Cluster: management-hypershift-lab Hosted Cluster: sno-hcp (namespace: clusters) Control Plane Namespace: clusters-sno-hcp

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This document captures the step-by-step process to configure OADP (OpenShift API for Data Protection) to backup HCP (Hosted Control Planes) including etcd data using ODF RGW as the S3 backend.

docs.title: Prerequisites Verified
docs.text: Requirement Status ODF installed ✅ RGW StorageClass available ✅ ocs-storagecluster-ceph-rgw etcd PVC using RBD ✅ data-etcd-0 (4Gi) VolumeSnapshotClass available ✅ ocs-storagecluster-rbdplugin-snapclass cluster-admin access ✅

docs.title: Step 1: Verify RGW S3 Storage
docs.text: Before setting up OADP, we verified that ODF RGW was working correctly.

docs.title: 1.1 Check RGW Pods
docs.text:
oc get pods -n openshift-storage | grep rgw
Result: rook-ceph-rgw-ocs-storagecluster-cephobjectstore-a-* running (2/2)

docs.title: 1.2 Check RGW StorageClass
docs.text:
oc get sc | grep rgw
Result: ocs-storagecluster-ceph-rgw available

docs.title: 1.3 Test S3 Connectivity
docs.text:
Created a test pod to verify S3 operations: 

# Create test pod with aws-cli
oc apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: rgw-s3-test
  namespace: odf-test
spec:
  containers:
  - name: aws-cli
    image: amazon/aws-cli:latest
    command: ["sleep", "3600"]
    env:
    - name: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID
      valueFrom:
        secretKeyRef:
          name: test-bucket
          key: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID
    - name: AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
      valueFrom:
        secretKeyRef:
          name: test-bucket
          key: AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
    - name: S3_ENDPOINT
      value: "https://rook-ceph-rgw-ocs-storagecluster-cephobjectstore.openshift-storage.svc:443"
    - name: S3_BUCKET
      valueFrom:
        configMapKeyRef:
          name: test-bucket
          key: BUCKET_NAME
  restartPolicy: Never
EOF

docs.title: 1.4 Verified S3 Operations
docs.text:
oc exec -n odf-test rgw-s3-test -- sh -c '
  # Upload
  echo "test" > /tmp/test.txt
  aws s3 cp /tmp/test.txt s3://$S3_BUCKET/ --endpoint-url $S3_ENDPOINT --no-verify-ssl

  # Download
  aws s3 cp s3://$S3_BUCKET/test.txt /tmp/downloaded.txt --endpoint-url $S3_ENDPOINT --no-verify-ssl

  # Delete
  aws s3 rm s3://$S3_BUCKET/test.txt --endpoint-url $S3_ENDPOINT --no-verify-ssl
'
Result: All operations successful ✅

docs.title: 1.5 Cleanup Test Pod
docs.text: oc delete pod rgw-s3-test -n odf-test

Result: openshift-adp-controller-manager-* running

docs.title: Step 3: Create RGW Bucket and Credentials
3.1 Run Credentials Setup Script
docs.text: ./scripts/setup-rgw-credentials.sh

docs.title: 3.2 What the Script Does
docs.text:
1. Creates ObjectBucketClaim oadp-hcp-bucket in openshift-adp namespace
  2. Waits for OBC to be bound
  3. Extracts credentials from OBC secret
  4. Creates cloud-credentials secret in Velero format

docs.title: 3.3 Created Resources
docs.text:
ObjectBucketClaim: 

apiVersion: objectbucket.io/v1alpha1
kind: ObjectBucketClaim
metadata:
  name: oadp-hcp-bucket
  namespace: openshift-adp
spec:
  generateBucketName: oadp-hcp-backup
  storageClassName: ocs-storagecluster-ceph-rgw

Bucket Created: oadp-hcp-backup-efc2a666-b4ac-42d7-bd6e-b6d70a85fd90

Credentials Secret: cloud-credentials (Velero format)

docs.title: 4.1 Run DPA Deployment Script
docs.text: ./scripts/deploy-dpa-rgw.sh

docs.title: 4.2 What the Script Does
docs.text:
1. Verifies prerequisites (OADP operator, credentials)
  2. Gets bucket name from OBC ConfigMap
  3. Deploys DPA with RGW configuration
  4. Waits for BackupStorageLocation to be available

docs.title: 4.3 DPA Configuration
docs.text:
apiVersion: oadp.openshift.io/v1alpha1
kind: DataProtectionApplication
metadata:
  name: hcp-dpa
  namespace: openshift-adp
spec:
  backupLocations:
    - velero:
        config:
          s3Url: https://rook-ceph-rgw-ocs-storagecluster-cephobjectstore.openshift-storage.svc:443
          s3ForcePathStyle: "true"
          insecureSkipTLSVerify: "true"  # Self-signed cert
          region: us-east-1
        credential:
          key: cloud
          name: cloud-credentials
        objectStorage:
          bucket: oadp-hcp-backup-efc2a666-b4ac-42d7-bd6e-b6d70a85fd90
          prefix: hcp-backups
        provider: aws
  configuration:
    nodeAgent:
      enable: true
      uploaderType: kopia
    velero:
      defaultPlugins:
        - openshift
        - aws
        - csi

docs.title: 4.4 Verify DPA Status
docs.text:
oc get dpa -n openshift-adp
oc get backupstoragelocation -n openshift-adp
Result: hcp-dpa-1 BackupStorageLocation is Available

docs.title: 5.1 Label VolumeSnapshotClass for Velero
docs.text:
For CSI snapshots to work with Velero, the VolumeSnapshotClass needs a label:

oc label volumesnapshotclass ocs-storagecluster-rbdplugin-snapclass \
  velero.io/csi-volumesnapshot-class=true

docs.title: 5.2 Verify Label
docs.text: oc get volumesnapshotclass ocs-storagecluster-rbdplugin-snapclass -o yaml | grep -A5 labels

docs.title: 6.1 Issue Discovered
docs.text: The backup template referenced storageLocation: default but the actual BackupStorageLocation was named hcp-dpa-1.

docs.title: 6.2 Fix Applied
docs.text:
Updated manifests/backup-control-plane.yaml.template: 

# Before
storageLocation: default

# After
storageLocation: hcp-dpa-1

Also updated the label: 

labels:
  velero.io/storage-location: hcp-dpa-1

docs.text: ./scripts/02-backup-control-plane.sh sno-hcp clusters

docs.title: 7.2 What the Script Does
docs.text:
1. Verifies HostedCluster exists
  2. Verifies control plane namespace exists
  3. Pauses HostedCluster reconciliation
  4. Creates Backup CR with CSI volume snapshots

Result: | Name | Status | Bytes | |------|--------|-------| | hcp-sno-hcp-20260119-132459-8hvxw | Completed | 417,748,384 (417 MB) |

docs.title: OADP HCP Restore Test Procedure
docs.text:
Date: 2026-01-19 Cluster: management-hypershift-lab Hosted Cluster: sno-hcp Control Plane Namespace: clusters-sno-hcp

⚠️ Note: This procedure was tested with SingleReplica etcd (1 pod). The HighlyAvailable (3 etcd) commands are documented but not yet tested. The same principles apply, but with 3 PVCs and 3 pods.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This document provides a step-by-step procedure to test OADP restore of the HCP control plane, including etcd data recovery.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• OADP installed and configured
  • Valid backup exists with etcd data
  • oc CLI with cluster-admin access
  • Hosted cluster kubeconfig available

docs.title: Verify Prerequisites
docs.text:
# Check OADP is ready
oc get dpa -n openshift-adp
oc get backupstoragelocation -n openshift-adp

# List available backups
oc get backup -n openshift-adp

# Verify backup includes etcd data (DataUpload completed)
oc get dataupload -n openshift-adp -l velero.io/backup-name=<backup-name>

docs.title: What OADP Backs Up
docs.text: Component Location Backup Method HostedCluster CR clusters namespace K8s resource NodePool CR clusters namespace K8s resource Secrets clusters + control plane namespace K8s resource ConfigMaps clusters + control plane namespace K8s resource etcd PVC (data-etcd-0) clusters-sno-hcp CSI Snapshot → S3

docs.title: Key Insight: etcd Data
docs.text:
The etcd PVC contains all hosted cluster data: - Namespaces - Deployments - ConfigMaps - Secrets - All Kubernetes resources in the hosted cluster

When you restore the etcd PVC, you restore the entire hosted cluster state.

docs.title: Why Simple Restore Doesn't Work
docs.text:
A restore with existingResourcePolicy: update: - Updates K8s resources on management cluster ✅ - Restores etcd PVC data to the volume ✅ - BUT: Running etcd pod doesn't reload the restored data ❌

The etcd pod has the data in memory and on its mounted volume. The restored data is written to the volume, but etcd doesn't know to reload it.

docs.title: Proper Restore Procedure
docs.text: To properly restore etcd data: 1. Scale down etcd (stop the pod) 2. Delete the etcd PVC (remove current data) 3. Run OADP restore (recreates PVC with backup data) 4. Scale up etcd (pod starts with restored data)

docs.title: Test Procedure: Full etcd Restore Test
Phase 1: Create Test Data
docs.text:
Create a marker in the hosted cluster that we can verify after restore.

# Extract hosted cluster kubeconfig
oc get secret sno-hcp-admin-kubeconfig -n clusters \
  -o jsonpath='{.data.kubeconfig}' | base64 -d > /tmp/sno-hcp-kubeconfig

# Create test ConfigMap in hosted cluster
KUBECONFIG=/tmp/sno-hcp-kubeconfig oc create configmap oadp-restore-test \
  -n default \
  --from-literal=test-key="restore-test-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)" \
  --from-literal=created="$(date)" \
  --from-literal=purpose="OADP restore verification"

# Verify it was created
KUBECONFIG=/tmp/sno-hcp-kubeconfig oc get configmap oadp-restore-test -n default -o yaml

Record the test-key value: restore-test-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS

docs.title: Phase 2: Take Backup with Test Data
docs.text:
cd ~/Documents/code/MYHOMELAB/hcp/DR

# Take backup (includes the test ConfigMap in etcd)
./scripts/02-backup-control-plane.sh sno-hcp clusters

Wait for backup to complete: 

# Watch backup progress
oc get backup -n openshift-adp -w

# Record backup name: hcp-sno-hcp-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS

Verify etcd data was captured: 

# Check DataUpload completed (should show ~400MB for etcd)
oc get dataupload -n openshift-adp -l velero.io/backup-name=<backup-name>

Resume reconciliation: 

oc patch hostedcluster sno-hcp -n clusters --type=merge -p '{"spec":{"pausedUntil":null}}'

docs.title: Phase 3: Delete Test Data (Simulate Corruption)
docs.text:
# Delete the test ConfigMap from hosted cluster
KUBECONFIG=/tmp/sno-hcp-kubeconfig oc delete configmap oadp-restore-test -n default

# Verify it's gone
KUBECONFIG=/tmp/sno-hcp-kubeconfig oc get configmap oadp-restore-test -n default
# Expected: Error from server (NotFound)

docs.title: Phase 4: Perform etcd Restore
docs.text:
This is the critical phase where we restore the etcd data.

export CONTROL_PLANE_NAMESPACE="clusters-sno-hcp"
export BACKUP_NAME="hcp-sno-hcp-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS"  # Use your actual backup name

docs.title: Determine etcd Replica Count
docs.text:
First, check your HCP availability policy to determine etcd replica count:

# Check HostedCluster availability policy
oc get hostedcluster sno-hcp -n clusters -o jsonpath='{.spec.controllerAvailabilityPolicy}'
Policy etcd Replicas PVCs to Delete SingleReplica 1 data-etcd-0 HighlyAvailable 3 data-etcd-0, data-etcd-1, data-etcd-2 
# Get current replica count
ETCD_REPLICAS=$(oc get statefulset etcd -n $CONTROL_PLANE_NAMESPACE -o jsonpath='{.spec.replicas}')
echo "etcd replicas: $ETCD_REPLICAS"

docs.title: Step 4.1: Pause HostedCluster
docs.text:
oc patch hostedcluster sno-hcp -n clusters --type=merge \
  -p '{"spec":{"pausedUntil":"true"}}'

# Verify
oc get hostedcluster sno-hcp -n clusters -o jsonpath='{.spec.pausedUntil}'
# Should show: true

docs.title: Step 4.2: Scale Down etcd
docs.text:
For SingleReplica (1 etcd): 

# Scale etcd to 0
oc scale -n $CONTROL_PLANE_NAMESPACE statefulset/etcd --replicas=0

# Wait for etcd pod to terminate
oc wait --for=delete pod/etcd-0 -n $CONTROL_PLANE_NAMESPACE --timeout=120s

# Verify no etcd pods
oc get pods -n $CONTROL_PLANE_NAMESPACE -l app=etcd
# Should show: No resources found

For HighlyAvailable (3 etcd): (not tested) 

# Scale etcd to 0
oc scale -n $CONTROL_PLANE_NAMESPACE statefulset/etcd --replicas=0

# Wait for all etcd pods to terminate
oc wait --for=delete pod/etcd-0 pod/etcd-1 pod/etcd-2 \
  -n $CONTROL_PLANE_NAMESPACE --timeout=120s

# Verify no etcd pods
oc get pods -n $CONTROL_PLANE_NAMESPACE -l app=etcd
# Should show: No resources found

⚠️ At this point, the hosted cluster API is DOWN. This is expected.

docs.title: Step 4.3: Delete etcd PVC(s)
docs.text:
For SingleReplica (1 etcd): 

# Delete the etcd PVC
oc delete pvc data-etcd-0 -n $CONTROL_PLANE_NAMESPACE

# Wait for deletion
oc get pvc -n $CONTROL_PLANE_NAMESPACE | grep etcd
# Should show nothing

For HighlyAvailable (3 etcd): (not tested) 

# Delete all etcd PVCs
oc delete pvc data-etcd-0 data-etcd-1 data-etcd-2 -n $CONTROL_PLANE_NAMESPACE

# Wait for deletion
oc get pvc -n $CONTROL_PLANE_NAMESPACE | grep etcd
# Should show nothing

docs.title: Step 4.4: Run OADP Restore
docs.text:
cd ~/Documents/code/MYHOMELAB/hcp/DR

# Run restore script
./scripts/04-restore-same-cluster.sh $BACKUP_NAME

# When prompted, type 'yes' to confirm

Monitor restore progress: 

# Watch restore status
oc get restore -n openshift-adp -w

# Check for DataDownload (etcd data being restored)
oc get datadownload -n openshift-adp

Wait for restore to complete (Phase: Completed)

docs.title: Step 4.5: Verify PVC is Restored
docs.text:
# Check etcd PVC exists
oc get pvc data-etcd-0 -n $CONTROL_PLANE_NAMESPACE

# Expected: Bound status

docs.title: Step 4.6: Scale Up etcd
docs.text:
For SingleReplica (1 etcd): 

# Scale etcd back up to 1
oc scale -n $CONTROL_PLANE_NAMESPACE statefulset/etcd --replicas=1

# Wait for etcd to be ready
oc wait --for=condition=Ready pod/etcd-0 -n $CONTROL_PLANE_NAMESPACE --timeout=300s

# Verify etcd is running
oc get pods -n $CONTROL_PLANE_NAMESPACE -l app=etcd

For HighlyAvailable (3 etcd): (not tested) 

# Scale etcd back up to 3
oc scale -n $CONTROL_PLANE_NAMESPACE statefulset/etcd --replicas=3

# Wait for all etcd pods to be ready
oc wait --for=condition=Ready pod/etcd-0 pod/etcd-1 pod/etcd-2 \
  -n $CONTROL_PLANE_NAMESPACE --timeout=300s

# Verify all etcd pods are running
oc get pods -n $CONTROL_PLANE_NAMESPACE -l app=etcd
# Should show: etcd-0, etcd-1, etcd-2 all Running

# Verify etcd cluster health
oc rsh -n $CONTROL_PLANE_NAMESPACE -c etcd etcd-0 etcdctl endpoint health --cluster

docs.title: Step 4.7: Resume HostedCluster
docs.text:
oc patch hostedcluster sno-hcp -n clusters --type=merge \

docs.text: This document outlines the Disaster Recovery (DR) procedures for Hosted Control Planes (HCP) managed on OpenShift. It covers backup strategies, recovery procedures, and testing guidelines.

  • Management cluster protection

docs.title: 1.2 Out of Scope

docs.title: 5.2 Procedure: Restore to Same Management Cluster
docs.text:
When to use: Data corruption, accidental deletion, rollback needed

Estimated time: 30-60 minutes

  1. Verify backup integrity 

    ./scripts/verify-backup.sh <backup-name>

  2. Pause cluster reconciliation (if not already paused) 

    oc patch hostedcluster <name> -n <ns> --type=merge \
  -p '{"spec":{"pausedUntil":"true"}}'

  3. Execute restore 

    ./scripts/04-restore-same-cluster.sh <backup-name>

  4. Resume reconciliation 

    oc patch hostedcluster <name> -n <ns> --type=merge \
  -p '{"spec":{"pausedUntil":null}}'

  5. Verify cluster health 

    oc get hostedcluster -A
oc get nodepool -A

docs.title: 5.3 Procedure: Restore to New Management Cluster
docs.text:
When to use: Management cluster unrecoverable, migration required

Estimated time: 2-4 hours

Prerequisites: - New management cluster with HyperShift Operator - OADP configured with same S3 storage - External DNS configured

  1. Prepare new management cluster 

    # Install OADP
./scripts/01-install-oadp.sh

# Configure same S3 backend
# (use same credentials and bucket)

  2. Verify backup is accessible 

    ./scripts/verify-backup.sh <backup-name>

  3. Execute cross-cluster restore 

    ./scripts/05-restore-new-cluster.sh <backup-name>

  4. Resume hosted cluster reconciliation 

    oc patch hostedcluster <name> -n <ns> --type=merge \
  -p '{"spec":{"pausedUntil":null}}'

  5. Delete resources from old cluster (if accessible) 

    # On OLD management cluster
oc delete hostedcluster <name> -n <ns>

docs.title: 1. Overview
docs.text:
You can maintain high availability (HA) of hosted control planes by implementing:

Action Description Recover etcd members Fix individual failing etcd pods Backup/Restore etcd Point-in-time recovery of cluster state Disaster Recovery Full cluster recovery to same or new management cluster

docs.title: When Management Cluster Components Fail
docs.text: Failed Component Control Plane Impact Data Plane Impact Management API Cannot modify cluster configuration ✅ No impact - workloads run etcd (management) Cannot modify cluster configuration ✅ No impact - workloads run HyperShift Operator Cannot create/modify hosted clusters ✅ No impact - workloads run Ingress Controller API access may be affected ✅ No impact - workloads run Entire Management Cluster Hosted cluster in read-only state ✅ No impact - workloads run

docs.text: Failed Component Impact Recovery Single etcd pod Quorum maintained, auto-recovery Wait for automatic recovery Two etcd pods Quorum lost, cluster degraded Immediate intervention required All etcd pods Cluster unavailable Restore from backup kube-apiserver Cannot access hosted cluster API Pod auto-restarts kube-controller-manager Workloads not reconciled Pod auto-restarts

docs.title: 3.1 Check etcd Cluster Status
docs.text:
In a highly available control plane, three etcd pods run as part of a StatefulSet.

# Set control plane namespace
export CONTROL_PLANE_NAMESPACE="clusters-<hosted-cluster-name>"

# Check etcd pods status
oc get pods -n ${CONTROL_PLANE_NAMESPACE} -l app=etcd

# Expected output (healthy):
# NAME     READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
# etcd-0   1/1     Running   0          24h
# etcd-1   1/1     Running   0          24h
# etcd-2   1/1     Running   0          24h

docs.title: 3.2 Check etcd Member Health
docs.text:
# Log into an etcd pod
oc rsh -n ${CONTROL_PLANE_NAMESPACE} -c etcd etcd-0

# Inside the pod, check endpoint health
etcdctl endpoint health --cluster

# Expected output (healthy):
# https://etcd-0...:2379 is healthy: successfully committed proposal
# https://etcd-1...:2379 is healthy: successfully committed proposal
# https://etcd-2...:2379 is healthy: successfully committed proposal

# Check member list
etcdctl member list -w table

# Exit pod
exit

docs.title: 3.3 Check etcd Database Size
docs.text:
# Check database size (should be < 8GB)
oc rsh -n ${CONTROL_PLANE_NAMESPACE} -c etcd etcd-0 \
  etcdctl endpoint status --cluster -w table
Metric Healthy Value Action if Exceeded DB Size < 8 GB Defragment or investigate Raft Term Stable High churn indicates issues Leader One leader Multiple indicates split-brain

docs.title: 4.2 Recover Single Failing etcd Pod
docs.text:
Use when: One etcd pod is failing but quorum (2/3) is maintained.

# Set variables
export CONTROL_PLANE_NAMESPACE="clusters-<hosted-cluster-name>"
export FAILED_POD="etcd-1"  # The failing pod

# Step 1: Verify the failing pod
oc get pods -n ${CONTROL_PLANE_NAMESPACE} -l app=etcd

# Step 2: Delete the failing pod (it will be recreated)
oc delete pod ${FAILED_POD} -n ${CONTROL_PLANE_NAMESPACE}

# Step 3: Wait for pod to be recreated
oc get pods -n ${CONTROL_PLANE_NAMESPACE} -l app=etcd -w

# Step 4: Verify etcd cluster health
oc rsh -n ${CONTROL_PLANE_NAMESPACE} -c etcd etcd-0 \
  etcdctl endpoint health --cluster

docs.title: 4.3 Recover Multiple Failing etcd Pods (Quorum Lost)
docs.text:
Use when: Multiple etcd pods are failing and quorum is lost.

⚠️ WARNING: This procedure deletes etcd data. Only use when you have a backup or the data is already corrupted.

# Set variables
export CONTROL_PLANE_NAMESPACE="clusters-<hosted-cluster-name>"

# Step 1: Scale down etcd StatefulSet to 0
oc scale -n ${CONTROL_PLANE_NAMESPACE} statefulset/etcd --replicas=0

# Step 2: Wait for pods to terminate
oc get pods -n ${CONTROL_PLANE_NAMESPACE} -l app=etcd -w

# Step 3: Delete the PVCs for failed members (keep etcd-0 if it has good data)
# ONLY delete PVCs for corrupted members
oc delete -n ${CONTROL_PLANE_NAMESPACE} pvc/data-etcd-1 pvc/data-etcd-2

# Step 4: Scale etcd back up
oc scale -n ${CONTROL_PLANE_NAMESPACE} statefulset/etcd --replicas=3

# Step 5: Wait for new pods and verify health
oc get pods -n ${CONTROL_PLANE_NAMESPACE} -l app=etcd -w

docs.title: 5. etcd Backup and Restore (On-Premise)
docs.text: For hosted clusters on bare metal or on-premise environments.

docs.title: 5.1 Taking an etcd Snapshot
docs.text:
# Set variables
export CONTROL_PLANE_NAMESPACE="clusters-<hosted-cluster-name>"
export BACKUP_DIR="/tmp/etcd-backup-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"

# Step 1: Create backup directory
mkdir -p ${BACKUP_DIR}

# Step 2: Get the etcd client endpoint
ETCD_ENDPOINT=$(oc get pods -n ${CONTROL_PLANE_NAMESPACE} etcd-0 \
  -o jsonpath='{.status.podIP}'):2379

# Step 3: Take snapshot from etcd-0
oc exec -n ${CONTROL_PLANE_NAMESPACE} etcd-0 -c etcd -- \
  etcdctl snapshot save /var/lib/data/snapshot.db

# Step 4: Copy snapshot to local machine
oc cp ${CONTROL_PLANE_NAMESPACE}/etcd-0:/var/lib/data/snapshot.db \
  ${BACKUP_DIR}/snapshot.db -c etcd

# Step 5: Verify snapshot
oc exec -n ${CONTROL_PLANE_NAMESPACE} etcd-0 -c etcd -- \
  etcdctl snapshot status /var/lib/data/snapshot.db -w table

# Step 6: Store backup safely
echo "Backup saved to: ${BACKUP_DIR}/snapshot.db"

docs.title: 5.2 Restoring from etcd Snapshot
docs.text:
⚠️ WARNING: Restoring etcd is a destructive operation. The cluster will be unavailable during restore.

# Set variables
export CONTROL_PLANE_NAMESPACE="clusters-<hosted-cluster-name>"
export SNAPSHOT_FILE="/path/to/snapshot.db"

# Step 1: Pause the HostedCluster
oc patch hostedcluster <name> -n clusters --type=merge \
  -p '{"spec":{"pausedUntil":"true"}}'

# Step 2: Scale down etcd
oc scale -n ${CONTROL_PLANE_NAMESPACE} statefulset/etcd --replicas=0

# Step 3: Wait for pods to terminate
oc wait --for=delete pod/etcd-0 pod/etcd-1 pod/etcd-2 \
  -n ${CONTROL_PLANE_NAMESPACE} --timeout=120s

# Step 4: Delete all etcd PVCs
oc delete pvc -n ${CONTROL_PLANE_NAMESPACE} \
  data-etcd-0 data-etcd-1 data-etcd-2

# Step 5: Copy snapshot to a temporary location accessible by the restore job
# (This depends on your storage setup - using a PVC or ConfigMap)

# Step 6: Create restore job (see manifests/etcd-restore-job.yaml)

# Step 7: Scale etcd back up
oc scale -n ${CONTROL_PLANE_NAMESPACE} statefulset/etcd --replicas=3

# Step 8: Resume the HostedCluster
oc patch hostedcluster <name> -n clusters --type=merge \
  -p '{"spec":{"pausedUntil":null}}'

# Step 9: Verify cluster health
oc get hostedcluster <name> -n clusters

docs.title: 6. etcd Backup and Restore (AWS)
docs.text: For hosted clusters on AWS with S3 storage.

docs.title: 6.1 Taking an etcd Snapshot on AWS
docs.text:
# Set variables
export CONTROL_PLANE_NAMESPACE="clusters-<hosted-cluster-name>"
export S3_BUCKET="your-etcd-backup-bucket"
export BACKUP_NAME="etcd-snapshot-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"

# Step 1: Take snapshot
oc exec -n ${CONTROL_PLANE_NAMESPACE} etcd-0 -c etcd -- \
  etcdctl snapshot save /var/lib/data/snapshot.db

  /tmp/snapshot.db -c etcd

aws s3 cp /tmp/snapshot.db s3://${S3_BUCKET}/${BACKUP_NAME}/snapshot.db

docs.title: HCP Restore Procedures
docs.text: Step-by-step restore procedures for Hosted Control Planes.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Backup verified and accessible
  • oc CLI installed and authenticated as cluster-admin
  • OADP Operator installed and configured
  • For cross-cluster restore: New management cluster prepared

docs.title: Verify Prerequisites
docs.text:
# Check OADP status
oc get dpa -n openshift-adp

# Verify backup exists
./scripts/verify-backup.sh <backup-name>

docs.title: Procedure 1: Restore to Same Management Cluster
docs.text:
Use when: Data corruption, accidental deletion, rollback to previous state

Estimated time: 30-60 minutes

docs.title: Step 1: Assess the Situation
docs.text: Document: - What happened: __ - Which cluster affected: __ - When did it occur: __ - Is the hosted cluster accessible: __

docs.title: Step 2: Select Backup to Restore
docs.text:
# List available backups
./scripts/verify-backup.sh

# Verify the backup you want to restore
./scripts/verify-backup.sh <backup-name>

Record: - Backup Name: __ - Backup Date: __ - Backup Status: ___

docs.title: Step 3: Pause Reconciliation (If Not Already)
docs.text:
# Pause HostedCluster
oc patch hostedcluster <name> -n <namespace> --type=merge \
  -p '{"spec":{"pausedUntil":"true"}}'

# Pause NodePools
oc patch nodepool <name> -n <namespace> --type=merge \
  -p '{"spec":{"pausedUntil":"true"}}'

docs.title: Step 4: Execute Restore
docs.text:
./scripts/04-restore-same-cluster.sh <backup-name>

The script will: 1. Verify backup exists and is completed 2. Show backup details 3. Ask for confirmation 4. Create Restore CR 5. Wait for completion

docs.title: Step 5: Monitor Restore Progress
docs.text:
# Watch restore status
oc get restore -n openshift-adp -w

# Get detailed status
oc describe restore restore-<backup-name>-<timestamp> -n openshift-adp

docs.title: Step 6: Verify Restore Completion
docs.text:
Check restore status: 

oc get restore -n openshift-adp

Expected: Phase: Completed

docs.title: Step 7: Resume Reconciliation
docs.text:
# Resume HostedCluster
oc patch hostedcluster <name> -n <namespace> --type=merge \
  -p '{"spec":{"pausedUntil":null}}'

# Resume NodePools
oc patch nodepool <name> -n <namespace> --type=merge \
  -p '{"spec":{"pausedUntil":null}}'

docs.title: Step 8: Verify Cluster Health
docs.text:
# Check HostedCluster status
oc get hostedcluster <name> -n <namespace> -o wide

# Verify Available=True
oc get hostedcluster <name> -n <namespace> \
  -o jsonpath='{.status.conditions[?(@.type=="Available")].status}'

# Check NodePool
oc get nodepool -n <namespace>

# Check control plane pods
oc get pods -n <namespace>-<cluster-name>

docs.title: Step 9: Verify Worker Nodes
docs.text:
# Get hosted cluster kubeconfig
oc get secret <name>-admin-kubeconfig -n <namespace> \
  -o jsonpath='{.data.kubeconfig}' | base64 -d > /tmp/hc-kubeconfig

# Check nodes on hosted cluster
KUBECONFIG=/tmp/hc-kubeconfig oc get nodes

docs.title: Step 10: Document Recovery
docs.text: Record: - Recovery Date/Time: __ - Backup Used: __ - Restore Name: __ - Duration: __ - Issues Encountered: __ - Operator: __

docs.title: Procedure 2: Restore to New Management Cluster
docs.text:
Use when: Original management cluster is unrecoverable, migration required

Estimated time: 2-4 hours

docs.title: Step 1: Prepare New Management Cluster
docs.text: Ensure the new cluster has: - [ ] OpenShift 4.14+ installed - [ ] HyperShift Operator installed - [ ] Network connectivity to worker nodes - [ ] External DNS configured (if using)

docs.title: Step 2: Install OADP on New Cluster
docs.text:
# On NEW management cluster
./scripts/01-install-oadp.sh

docs.title: Step 3: Configure Same S3 Backend
docs.text:
Use the same S3 credentials and bucket as the source cluster:

# Apply credentials secret (same values as source)
oc apply -f manifests/04-credentials-secret.yaml

# Apply DPA with same S3 configuration
export S3_BUCKET="<same-bucket>"
export S3_ENDPOINT="<same-endpoint>"
export S3_REGION="<same-region>"
envsubst < manifests/05-dpa.yaml.template | oc apply -f -

docs.title: Step 4: Wait for Backup Sync
docs.text:
# Wait for OADP to sync backups from S3
oc wait --for=jsonpath='{.status.phase}'=Available \
  backupstoragelocation/default -n openshift-adp --timeout=300s

# Verify backup is visible
./scripts/verify-backup.sh <backup-name>

docs.title: Step 5: Execute Cross-Cluster Restore
docs.text: ./scripts/05-restore-new-cluster.sh <backup-name>

docs.title: Step 6: Monitor Restore
docs.text: oc get restore -n openshift-adp -w

docs.title: Step 7: Resume Reconciliation on New Cluster
docs.text:
# Resume HostedCluster
oc patch hostedcluster <name> -n <namespace> --type=merge \
  -p '{"spec":{"pausedUntil":null}}'

# Resume NodePools
oc patch nodepool <name> -n <namespace> --type=merge \
  -p '{"spec":{"pausedUntil":null}}'

docs.title: Step 8: Verify Control Plane Starts
docs.text:
# Watch control plane pods come up
oc get pods -n <namespace>-<cluster-name> -w

# Check HostedCluster becomes Available
oc get hostedcluster <name> -n <namespace> -w

docs.title: Step 9: Update DNS (If Using External DNS)
docs.text:
If using external DNS, it should automatically update. Verify:

# Check DNS resolution
dig api.<cluster-name>.<base-domain>

# Should resolve to new cluster's ingress

docs.title: Step 10: Clean Up Old Cluster (If Accessible)
docs.text:
IMPORTANT: Only do this AFTER verifying the restore is successful!

# On OLD management cluster (if accessible)
oc delete hostedcluster <name> -n <namespace> --wait=false

# Force delete if stuck
oc patch hostedcluster <name> -n <namespace> \
  --type=merge -p '{"metadata":{"finalizers":[]}}'

docs.title: Step 11: Document Recovery
docs.text: Record: - Source Cluster: __ - Destination Cluster: __ - Backup Used: __ - Recovery Time: __ - Issues Encountered: ___

docs.title: Restore Stuck in "InProgress"
docs.text:
# Check restore details
oc describe restore <restore-name> -n openshift-adp

# Check velero logs
oc logs -n openshift-adp -l app.kubernetes.io/name=velero

# Check for PVC restore issues
oc get pvc -n <control-plane-namespace>

docs.title: Restore Failed
docs.text:
# Get failure reason
oc get restore <restore-name> -n openshift-adp \
  -o jsonpath='{.status.failureReason}'

# Check detailed logs
velero restore logs <restore-name>

docs.title: HostedCluster Not Becoming Available
docs.text:
# Check HostedCluster conditions
oc get hostedcluster <name> -n <namespace> -o yaml

# Check control plane pods
oc get pods -n <namespace>-<cluster-name>

# Check etcd logs
oc logs -n <namespace>-<cluster-name> -l app=etcd

docs.title: Workers Not Joining
docs.text:
# Check NodePool status
oc get nodepool <name> -n <namespace> -o yaml

# Check agent machines
oc get agentmachine -n <namespace>-<cluster-name>

# On hosted cluster, check nodes
KUBECONFIG=/tmp/hc-kubeconfig oc get nodes
KUBECONFIG=/tmp/hc-kubeconfig oc get csr

docs.title: Conflict with Old Cluster
docs.text:
If both clusters try to manage the same hosted cluster:

  1. Stop reconciliation on old cluster immediately: 

    # On OLD cluster
oc patch hostedcluster <name> -n <namespace> --type=merge \
  -p '{"spec":{"pausedUntil":"true"}}'

  2. Delete from old cluster: 

    oc delete hostedcluster <name> -n <namespace>

docs.title: If Restore Fails Mid-Way
docs.text:
1. Delete partial restore resources: 

    oc delete restore <restore-name> -n openshift-adp

  2. Clean up any partially restored resources: 

    oc delete hostedcluster <name> -n <namespace> --ignore-not-found
oc delete namespace <namespace>-<cluster-name> --ignore-not-found

  3. Try restore again with different backup if available

docs.title: Where is the Data Stored?
docs.text:
Important: The data is NOT stored in the pod filesystem!

  • Data is stored in Ceph RGW (RADOS Gateway) object storage backend
  • RGW stores objects in Ceph RADOS pools (distributed across OSDs)
  • The pod only accesses data via S3 API calls
  • Data persists even if the pod is deleted
  • Data is replicated according to Ceph pool replication settings

docs.title: How to Use RGW S3 Storage
Method 1: Use the Test Pod (Already Configured)
docs.text:
# Exec into the test pod
oc exec -it test-rgw -n app-fullstack -- bash

# Environment variables are already set:
# - AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID
# - AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
# - S3_BUCKET
# - S3_ENDPOINT

# List files
aws s3 ls s3://$S3_BUCKET/ \
  --endpoint-url https://$S3_ENDPOINT \
  --no-verify-ssl

# Upload a file
echo "My data" > /tmp/myfile.txt
aws s3 cp /tmp/myfile.txt s3://$S3_BUCKET/ \
  --endpoint-url https://$S3_ENDPOINT \
  --no-verify-ssl

# Download a file
aws s3 cp s3://$S3_BUCKET/myfile.txt /tmp/downloaded.txt \
  --endpoint-url https://$S3_ENDPOINT \
  --no-verify-ssl

# Delete a file
aws s3 rm s3://$S3_BUCKET/myfile.txt \
  --endpoint-url https://$S3_ENDPOINT \
  --no-verify-ssl

docs.title: Method 2: Create Your Own Application with S3 Access
docs.text:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: my-s3-app
  namespace: app-fullstack
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: my-app-image
    env:
    # Load credentials from the Secret
    - name: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID
      valueFrom:
        secretKeyRef:
          name: test-rgw-bucket
          key: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID
    - name: AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
      valueFrom:
        secretKeyRef:
          name: test-rgw-bucket
          key: AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
    # Load config from the ConfigMap
    - name: S3_BUCKET
      valueFrom:
        configMapKeyRef:
          name: test-rgw-bucket
          key: BUCKET_NAME
    - name: S3_ENDPOINT
      valueFrom:
        configMapKeyRef:
          name: test-rgw-bucket
          key: BUCKET_HOST
    - name: S3_PORT
      valueFrom:
        configMapKeyRef:
          name: test-rgw-bucket
          key: BUCKET_PORT

docs.title: Method 3: Mount Credentials as Files
docs.text:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: my-s3-app
  namespace: app-fullstack
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: my-app-image
    volumeMounts:
    - name: s3-credentials
      mountPath: /s3-credentials
      readOnly: true
    - name: s3-config
      mountPath: /s3-config
      readOnly: true
  volumes:
  - name: s3-credentials
    secret:
      secretName: test-rgw-bucket
  - name: s3-config
    configMap:
      name: test-rgw-bucket

Then in your application: 

export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=$(cat /s3-credentials/AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID)
export AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=$(cat /s3-credentials/AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY)
export S3_BUCKET=$(cat /s3-config/BUCKET_NAME)
export S3_ENDPOINT=$(cat /s3-config/BUCKET_HOST)

docs.title: Create Additional Buckets
docs.text:
apiVersion: objectbucket.io/v1alpha1
kind: ObjectBucketClaim
metadata:
  name: my-new-bucket
  namespace: my-namespace
spec:
  generateBucketName: my-new-bucket
  storageClassName: ocs-storagecluster-ceph-rgw

This will automatically create: - A new S3 bucket - A Secret: my-new-bucket (with credentials) - A ConfigMap: my-new-bucket (with bucket name and endpoint)

docs.title: Using S3 from Outside the Cluster
docs.text:
To access RGW from outside OpenShift, you need to expose it via a Route:

# Check if RGW route exists
oc get route -n openshift-storage | grep rgw

# If not, create one:
oc create route edge rgw-external \
  --service=rook-ceph-rgw-ocs-storagecluster-cephobjectstore \
  --port=http \
  -n openshift-storage

# Get the external URL
oc get route rgw-external -n openshift-storage -o jsonpath='{.spec.host}'

Then use the external hostname as your S3 endpoint.

docs.title: Connection Issues
docs.text: If you get "Connection was closed" errors: - Use HTTPS instead of HTTP: --endpoint-url https://... - Add --no-verify-ssl flag (self-signed cert)

docs.title: Slow Performance
docs.text: RGW performance depends on: - Underlying Ceph OSD performance - Network latency - Object size (smaller objects = more overhead)

# Check RGW logs

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
homelab-server.example.com (192.0.2.107)
├── Management Cluster (untouched)
│   └── 6 VMs on br-hypershift (192.168.125.x)
│
└── SNO Test Environment (sno-test network: 198.51.100.0/24, ISOLATED)
    │
    │  ⚠️  ISOLATED NETWORK - NO INTERNET ACCESS FOR VMs
    │
    ├── mirror-registry VM (198.51.100.141)
    │   ├── 2 vCPU, 6GB RAM, 200GB disk
    │   ├── Quay-based registry on port 8443
    │   └── ❌ NO internet access (truly isolated)
    │
    └── sno-disconnected VM (198.51.100.60)
        ├── 8 vCPU, 16GB RAM, 120GB disk
        ├── Single Node OpenShift 4.20.8 (upgraded from 4.18.14)
        └── ❌ NO internet access (truly isolated)

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Access to homelab-server.example.com via SSH
  • Red Hat pull-secret (saved in pull-secret.json)
  • kcli installed on homelab-server

docs.title: Phase 1: Create Isolated Network
docs.text:
# SSH to homelab-server
ssh lab-user@homelab-server.example.com

# Create ISOLATED network for SNO test (--isolated = NO NAT, NO INTERNET)
kcli create network -c 198.51.100.0/24 --domain example.local --isolated sno-test

# Verify network is isolated (should NOT show 'nat')
kcli list network | grep sno-test
# Expected: sno-test | routed | 198.51.100.0/24 | True | example.local | isolated

# Add DNS entries for mirror-registry and SNO
sudo virsh net-update sno-test add dns-host \
  "<host ip=\"198.51.100.141\">
    <hostname>mirror-registry.example.local</hostname>
    <hostname>mirror-registry</hostname>
  </host>" --live --config

sudo virsh net-update sno-test add dns-host \
  "<host ip=\"198.51.100.60\">
    <hostname>sno-disconnected.example.local</hostname>
    <hostname>api.sno-disconnected.example.local</hostname>
    <hostname>api-int.sno-disconnected.example.local</hostname>
  </host>" --live --config

# Verify network
kcli list network

docs.title: Phase 2: Create Mirror Registry VM
docs.text:
# Use 6GB RAM (4GB causes memory pressure during large mirror operations)
kcli create vm \
  -P numcpus=2 \
  -P memory=6144 \
  -P disks=[150] \
  -P nets=[sno-test] \
  -P image=centos9stream \
  mirror-registry

# Wait for IP assignment
sleep 30
MIRROR_IP=$(kcli info vm mirror-registry -f ip -v)
echo "Mirror Registry IP: ${MIRROR_IP}"

docs.title: Phase 3: Install mirror-registry Tool
docs.text:
# SSH to mirror-registry VM
kcli ssh mirror-registry

# Install podman
sudo dnf install -y podman

# Download mirror-registry tool
curl -L -o mirror-registry.tar.gz \
  https://mirror.openshift.com/pub/openshift-v4/clients/mirror-registry/1.3.11/mirror-registry.tar.gz
tar -xzf mirror-registry.tar.gz

# Fix cgroup configuration (required for VMs)
sudo mkdir -p /etc/containers/containers.conf.d
cat << 'EOF' | sudo tee /etc/containers/containers.conf.d/cgroups.conf
[engine]
cgroup_manager = "cgroupfs"
EOF

# Install mirror-registry (save the password!)
sudo ./mirror-registry install \
  --quayHostname mirror-registry.example.local \
  --quayRoot /opt/quay

# IMPORTANT: Configure Quay for OCP mirroring
cat << 'EOF' | sudo tee -a /opt/quay/quay-config/config.yaml

# Allow large OCP image layers (default 5MB causes 413 errors)
MAXIMUM_LAYER_SIZE: 20G

# Enable automatic pruning of old tags
FEATURE_AUTO_PRUNE: true
EOF

# Restart Quay to apply the changes
sudo podman restart quay-app quay-postgres quay-redis
sleep 30

# Verify registry is working
curl -sk https://localhost:8443/v2/_catalog

exit

Note: - MAXIMUM_LAYER_SIZE: 20G - Required for OCP image layers (default 5MB causes HTTP 413 errors) - FEATURE_AUTO_PRUNE: true - Enables automatic cleanup of old image tags

docs.title: Phase 4: Configure homelab-server for oc-mirror
docs.text:
# On homelab-server
mkdir -p ~/oc-mirror-workspace

# Add registry to /etc/hosts
echo "198.51.100.141 mirror-registry.example.local" | sudo tee -a /etc/hosts

# Get CA certificate from mirror-registry
kcli ssh mirror-registry "sudo cat /opt/quay/quay-rootCA/rootCA.pem" \
  > ~/oc-mirror-workspace/mirror-registry-ca.pem

# Add CA to system trust
sudo cp ~/oc-mirror-workspace/mirror-registry-ca.pem /etc/pki/ca-trust/source/anchors/

curl -sL https://mirror.openshift.com/pub/openshift-v4/x86_64/clients/ocp/stable/oc-mirror.tar.gz \
  -o /tmp/oc-mirror.tar.gz

sudo chmod +x /usr/local/bin/oc-mirror

docs.text:
cd ~/oc-mirror-workspace

# Copy your Red Hat pull-secret to pull-secret-rh.json

MIRROR_PASSWORD="<your-mirror-registry-password>"
MIRROR_AUTH=$(echo -n "init:${MIRROR_PASSWORD}" | base64 -w0)

jq --arg auth "$MIRROR_AUTH" \
  '.auths += {"mirror-registry.example.local:8443": {"auth": $auth}}' \
  pull-secret-rh.json > pull-secret.json

docs.text:

apiVersion: mirror.openshift.io/v2alpha1
kind: ImageSetConfiguration
mirror:
  platform:
    architectures:
      - amd64
    channels:
      - name: stable-4.18
        minVersion: 4.18.14
        maxVersion: 4.18.14
    graph: true

  operators:
    - catalog: registry.redhat.io/redhat/redhat-operator-index:v4.18
      packages:
        - name: cincinnati-operator
          channels:
            - name: v1
EOF

docs.text:

oc mirror --v2 \
  --config imageset-config.yaml \
  docker://mirror-registry.example.local:8443/ocp4 \
  --workspace file://./workspace \
  --authfile pull-secret.json

# Verify generated resources
ls -la workspace/working-dir/cluster-resources/

  --tools \
  --from=mirror-registry.example.local:8443/ocp4/openshift/release-images:4.18.14-x86_64 \
  --to=/tmp/ocp-tools \
  --registry-config=/home/lab-user/oc-mirror-workspace/pull-secret.json

cd ~/sno-disconnected

# Create install-config.yaml
cat > install-config.yaml << 'EOF'
apiVersion: v1
baseDomain: example.local
metadata:

networking:
  networkType: OVNKubernetes

  - cidr: 10.128.0.0/14

- name: worker

pullSecret: '<PULL_SECRET_JSON_INLINE>'

docs.title: Phase 18: Install Cincinnati Operator (OSUS)
docs.text:
export KUBECONFIG=~/sno-disconnected/auth/kubeconfig

# Create namespace
oc create namespace openshift-update-service

# Create OperatorGroup
cat << EOF | oc apply -f -
apiVersion: operators.coreos.com/v1
kind: OperatorGroup
metadata:
  name: openshift-update-service
  namespace: openshift-update-service
spec:
  targetNamespaces:
  - openshift-update-service
EOF

# Create Subscription
cat << EOF | oc apply -f -
apiVersion: operators.coreos.com/v1alpha1
kind: Subscription
metadata:
  name: cincinnati-operator
  namespace: openshift-update-service
spec:
  channel: v1
  installPlanApproval: Automatic
  name: cincinnati-operator
  source: cs-redhat-operator-index-v4-18
  sourceNamespace: openshift-marketplace
EOF

# Wait for operator to be ready
oc get csv -n openshift-update-service -w

# Apply the generated UpdateService config
oc apply -f ~/oc-mirror-workspace/workspace/working-dir/cluster-resources/updateService.yaml

# Or create manually:
cat << EOF | oc apply -f -
apiVersion: updateservice.operator.openshift.io/v1
kind: UpdateService
metadata:
  name: update-service-oc-mirror
  namespace: openshift-update-service
spec:
  graphDataImage: mirror-registry.example.local:8443/ocp4/openshift/graph-image:latest
  releases: mirror-registry.example.local:8443/ocp4/openshift/release-images
  replicas: 1
EOF

# Check status
oc get updateservice -n openshift-update-service
oc get pods -n openshift-update-service

docs.title: Phase 20: Configure Cluster to Use OSUS
docs.text:
export KUBECONFIG=~/sno-disconnected/auth/kubeconfig

# Get OSUS route
OSUS_ROUTE=$(oc get route -n openshift-update-service -o jsonpath='{.items[0].spec.host}')
echo "OSUS URL: https://${OSUS_ROUTE}/api/upgrades_info/v1/graph"

# Get OSUS CA certificate
oc get secret -n openshift-update-service update-service-oc-mirror-tls -o jsonpath='{.data.tls\.crt}' | base64 -d > osus-ca.crt

# Create configmap for CA
oc create configmap osus-ca --from-file=updateservice-registry=osus-ca.crt -n openshift-config

# Patch clusterversion to use OSUS
oc patch clusterversion version --type merge -p "{
  \"spec\": {
    \"upstream\": \"https://${OSUS_ROUTE}/api/upgrades_info/v1/graph\",
    \"channel\": \"stable-4.18\"
  }
}"

# Add CA to cluster proxy
oc patch proxy cluster --type merge -p '{"spec":{"trustedCA":{"name":"osus-ca"}}}'

# Verify upgrade paths
oc adm upgrade

docs.title: Configure HTPasswd Authentication (Optional)
docs.text: By default, the cluster uses the kubeadmin user. For better user management, configure HTPasswd authentication:

docs.title: Option 1: Use the Script (Recommended)
docs.text:
# SSH to homelab-server
ssh lab-user@homelab-server.example.com

# Login to the cluster as kubeadmin
export KUBECONFIG=~/sno-disconnected/auth/kubeconfig
oc whoami

# Run the configure script
cd ~/MYHOMELAB  # or wherever repo is cloned
./sno-disconnected/scripts/configure-htpasswd.sh

The script will: 1. Prompt for admin and developer passwords 2. Create the htpasswd secret in openshift-config namespace 3. Configure OAuth identity provider 4. Grant cluster-admin to the admin user 5. Wait for OAuth pods to restart

Script Options: 

# Only create admin user (no developer)
./sno-disconnected/scripts/configure-htpasswd.sh --admin-only

# Read users from file
./sno-disconnected/scripts/configure-htpasswd.sh --users users.txt

Users file format: 

admin:secretpassword
developer:devpass123
# Comments start with #

docs.title: Option 2: Manual Configuration
docs.text:
# 1. Create htpasswd file
htpasswd -cbB /tmp/htpasswd admin 'yourpassword'
htpasswd -bB /tmp/htpasswd developer 'devpassword'

# 2. Create secret in openshift-config namespace
oc create secret generic htpasswd-secret \
  --from-file=htpasswd=/tmp/htpasswd \
  -n openshift-config

# 3. Clean up temp file
rm /tmp/htpasswd

# 4. Apply OAuth configuration
oc apply -f sno-disconnected/manifests/oauth-htpasswd.yaml

# 5. Grant cluster-admin to admin user (htpasswd users have NO roles by default!)
oc adm policy add-cluster-role-to-user cluster-admin admin

# 6. Wait for OAuth pods to restart
oc get pods -n openshift-authentication -w

docs.title: prune-mirror-registry.sh
docs.text:
Clean up old OCP versions from the mirror registry after successful upgrades. For example, remove 4.18 content after upgrading to 4.19.

Location: scripts/prune-mirror-registry.sh

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
cd ~/oc-mirror-workspace

# Ensure imageset-config.yaml ONLY contains versions you want to KEEP
# Remove old version references before running prune

docs.title: Check Disk Space
docs.text:
./prune-mirror-registry.sh --check

Shows disk usage on mirror-registry VM and current versions in imageset-config.yaml.

docs.title: Dry Run (Preview)
docs.text:
./prune-mirror-registry.sh --dry-run

Generates delete manifests showing what WOULD be deleted. Always run this first.

docs.title: Execute Delete
docs.text:
./prune-mirror-registry.sh --execute

Deletes images from registry. Requires prior --dry-run. Prompts for confirmation.

docs.title: Garbage Collection
docs.text:
./prune-mirror-registry.sh --gc

Runs registry garbage collection to reclaim disk space after deleting images.

docs.title: Full Cleanup (Automated)
docs.text:
./prune-mirror-registry.sh --full

Runs dry-run + execute + garbage collection in sequence. Use with caution.

docs.title: Typical Workflow After Upgrade
docs.text:
# 1. Update imageset-config.yaml - remove old versions
#    e.g., remove stable-4.18, change v4.18 catalog to v4.19

# 2. Preview what will be deleted
./prune-mirror-registry.sh --dry-run

# 3. Review the manifest
cat ~/oc-mirror-workspace/delete-workspace/working-dir/delete/delete-images.yaml

# 4. Execute if satisfied
./prune-mirror-registry.sh --execute

# 5. Reclaim disk space
./prune-mirror-registry.sh --gc

# 6. Verify space recovered
./prune-mirror-registry.sh --check

docs.title: Phase 21: Cincinnati Operator (OSUS) Installation
docs.text:
Date: December 2025

The Cincinnati Operator provides the OpenShift Update Service (OSUS) for disconnected clusters.

docs.title: Step 1: Create Namespace
docs.text:
export KUBECONFIG=~/sno-disconnected/auth/kubeconfig

oc create namespace openshift-update-service
# Or with annotations:
cat << EOF | oc apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: openshift-update-service
  annotations:
    openshift.io/node-selector: ""
  labels:
    openshift.io/cluster-monitoring: "true"
EOF

docs.title: Step 2: Create OperatorGroup
docs.text:
cat << EOF | oc apply -f -
apiVersion: operators.coreos.com/v1
kind: OperatorGroup
metadata:
  name: update-service-operator-group
  namespace: openshift-update-service
spec:
  targetNamespaces:
    - openshift-update-service
EOF

docs.title: Step 3: Create Subscription
docs.text:
cat << EOF | oc apply -f -
apiVersion: operators.coreos.com/v1alpha1
kind: Subscription
metadata:
  name: cincinnati-operator
  namespace: openshift-update-service
spec:
  channel: v1
  installPlanApproval: Automatic
  name: cincinnati-operator
  source: redhat-operators
  sourceNamespace: openshift-marketplace
EOF

docs.title: Step 4: Verify Installation
docs.text:
# Check CSV status (wait for Succeeded)
oc get csv -n openshift-update-service
# Expected: update-service-operator.v5.0.3  Succeeded

# Check operator pod
oc get pods -n openshift-update-service
# Expected: updateservice-operator-xxx  1/1 Running

# Verify CRD exists
oc get crd | grep updateservice
# Expected: updateservices.updateservice.operator.openshift.io

docs.title: Result
docs.text: Component Status Namespace openshift-update-service created OperatorGroup update-service-operator-group created Subscription cincinnati-operator (channel: v1) CSV update-service-operator.v5.0.3 - Succeeded Pod updateservice-operator - Running

docs.title: Step 1: Create CA ConfigMap
docs.text:
The UpdateService needs to trust the mirror-registry's self-signed certificate:

export KUBECONFIG=~/sno-disconnected/auth/kubeconfig

# Create ConfigMap with mirror-registry CA
cat << EOF | oc apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: mirror-registry-ca
  namespace: openshift-config
data:
  updateservice-registry: |
$(cat ~/oc-mirror-workspace/mirror-registry-ca.pem | sed 's/^/    /')
  mirror-registry.example.local..8443: |
$(cat ~/oc-mirror-workspace/mirror-registry-ca.pem | sed 's/^/    /')
EOF

# Configure cluster to trust this CA
oc patch image.config.openshift.io/cluster --type=merge \
  -p '{"spec":{"additionalTrustedCA":{"name":"mirror-registry-ca"}}}'

docs.title: Step 2: Deploy UpdateService CR
docs.text:
# Use oc-mirror generated file (modified for SNO - 1 replica)
cat << EOF | oc apply -f -
apiVersion: updateservice.operator.openshift.io/v1
kind: UpdateService
metadata:
  name: update-service-oc-mirror
  namespace: openshift-update-service
spec:
  graphDataImage: mirror-registry.example.local:8443/ocp4/openshift/graph-image:latest
  releases: mirror-registry.example.local:8443/ocp4/openshift/release-images
  replicas: 1
EOF

# Wait for pods to be ready
oc get pods -n openshift-update-service -w
# Wait until: update-service-oc-mirror-xxx  2/2  Running

docs.title: Step 3: Verify UpdateService
docs.text:
# Check UpdateService status
oc get updateservice -n openshift-update-service
oc describe updateservice update-service-oc-mirror -n openshift-update-service

# Get OSUS endpoint
oc get updateservice update-service-oc-mirror -n openshift-update-service \
  -o jsonpath='{.status.policyEngineURI}'

# Test graph endpoint (from within cluster)
oc exec -n openshift-update-service deploy/updateservice-operator -- \
  curl -s "http://update-service-oc-mirror-policy-engine:80/api/upgrades_info/v1/graph?channel=stable-4.18"

docs.title: Step 4: Configure Cluster to Use OSUS
docs.text:
OSUS_URI=$(oc get updateservice update-service-oc-mirror -n openshift-update-service \
  -o jsonpath='{.status.policyEngineURI}')

oc patch clusterversion version --type merge \
  -p "{\"spec\":{\"upstream\":\"${OSUS_URI}/api/upgrades_info/v1/graph\"}}"

# Verify
oc get clusterversion version -o jsonpath='{.spec.upstream}'

docs.title: Step 5: Check Available Upgrades
docs.text:
oc adm upgrade

# Expected output:
# Cluster version is 4.18.14
# Upstream: https://update-service-oc-mirror-route-openshift-update-service.apps.sno-disconnected.example.local/api/upgrades_info/v1/graph
# Channel: stable-4.18
# No updates available (because only 4.18.14 was mirrored)

docs.title: Result
docs.text:
Component Status UpdateService CR update-service-oc-mirror created Pods update-service-oc-mirror-xxx 2/2 Running Graph Data 1 node (4.18.14), 0 edges Cluster Upstream Configured to use OSUS

Note: To see available upgrades, mirror additional versions (e.g., 4.18.15, 4.18.16) using oc-mirror.

docs.title: Phase 23: Incremental Mirroring for Upgrades
docs.text:
Date: December 11, 2025

This phase demonstrates mirroring additional OCP versions to enable cluster upgrades.

docs.title: Step 1: Update ImageSetConfiguration
docs.text:
Edit the imageset-config.yaml to include new versions:

cd ~/oc-mirror-workspace

cat > imageset-config.yaml << 'EOF'
apiVersion: mirror.openshift.io/v2alpha1
kind: ImageSetConfiguration
mirror:
  platform:
    architectures:
      - amd64
    channels:
      - name: stable-4.18
        minVersion: 4.18.14
        maxVersion: 4.18.16    # <-- Increased from 4.18.14
    graph: true

  operators:
    - catalog: registry.redhat.io/redhat/redhat-operator-index:v4.18
      packages:
        - name: cincinnati-operator
          channels:
            - name: v1
EOF

docs.title: Step 2: Run Incremental oc-mirror
docs.text:
cd ~/oc-mirror-workspace

oc mirror --v2 \
  --config imageset-config.yaml \
  docker://mirror-registry.example.local:8443/ocp4 \
  --workspace file://./workspace \
  --authfile pull-secret.json

# Expected output:
# ✓ 568 / 568 release images mirrored successfully
# ✓ 5 / 5 operator images mirrored successfully
# mirror time: ~18 minutes

docs.title: Step 3: Restart OSUS to Refresh Graph
docs.text:
export KUBECONFIG=~/sno-disconnected/auth/kubeconfig

# Delete UpdateService pods to force graph refresh
oc delete pods -n openshift-update-service -l app=update-service-oc-mirror

# Wait for pods to restart
oc get pods -n openshift-update-service -w
# Wait for: update-service-oc-mirror-xxx  2/2  Running

docs.title: Step 4: Verify New Versions in Graph
docs.text:
# Check graph-builder logs for new releases
oc logs -n openshift-update-service deploy/update-service-oc-mirror -c graph-builder | tail -5
# Expected: graph update completed, 38 valid releases (was 34)

# Query graph for available versions
oc run curl-test --rm -it --restart=Never \
  --image=registry.access.redhat.com/ubi8/ubi-minimal -- \
  curl -s "http://update-service-oc-mirror-policy-engine.openshift-update-service.svc:80/api/upgrades_info/v1/graph?channel=stable-4.18"

docs.title: Step 5: Check Available Upgrades
docs.text:
oc adm upgrade

# Expected output shows:
# Cluster version is 4.18.14
# Upstream: https://update-service-oc-mirror-route-openshift-update-service...
# Available updates: 4.18.15, 4.18.16

docs.title: Step 6: Trigger Upgrade (Optional)
docs.text:
# Upgrade to specific version
oc adm upgrade --to=4.18.15

# Monitor upgrade progress
oc get clusterversion -w

# Check cluster operators during upgrade
oc get co

docs.title: Troubleshooting: 413 Request Entity Too Large
docs.text:
During mirroring, some large images may fail with HTTP 413 error:

error: writing blob: uploading layer chunked: StatusCode: 413

Solution: Retry the mirroring command multiple times. Each retry will continue from where it left off:

# Retry 1
oc mirror --v2 --config imageset-config.yaml docker://mirror-registry.example.local:8443/ocp4 ...

# Retry 2 (if needed)
oc mirror --v2 --config imageset-config.yaml docker://mirror-registry.example.local:8443/ocp4 ...

# Progress example:
# Retry 1: 180/568 images
# Retry 2: 330/568 images
# Retry 3: 568/568 images ✓

docs.title: Troubleshooting: Port 55000 Already Bound
docs.text:
If oc-mirror fails with "55000 is already bound":

# Find and kill the hanging process
ss -tlnp | grep 55000
# LISTEN  *:55000  users:(("oc-mirror",pid=103193,fd=8))

kill <pid>

# Retry mirroring
oc mirror --v2 ...

docs.title: Result
docs.text: Item Before After Mirrored OCP versions 4.18.14 4.18.14, 4.18.15, 4.18.16 Release images 190 568 Graph releases 34 38 Available upgrades None 4.18.15, 4.18.16

docs.title: Problem: OSUS Route TLS Certificate Not Trusted
docs.text:
After configuring OSUS, the cluster couldn't see available upgrades:

warning: Cannot display available updates:
  Reason: RemoteFailed
  Message: Unable to retrieve available updates: tls: failed to verify certificate: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority

Root Cause: The ClusterVersion operator couldn't verify the OSUS route's TLS certificate (signed by the cluster's ingress CA).

docs.title: Step 1: Add DNS Entry for OSUS Route
docs.text:
# On homelab-server - add OSUS route to /etc/hosts
sudo sed -i '/apps.sno-disconnected/s/$/ update-service-oc-mirror-route-openshift-update-service.apps.sno-disconnected.example.local/' /etc/hosts

docs.title: Step 2: Create CA Bundle ConfigMap
docs.text:
The additionalTrustedCA in image.config.openshift.io/cluster only applies to image registries, not HTTPS connections. For OSUS, we need to add the ingress CA to the cluster's proxy trusted CA:

export KUBECONFIG=~/sno-disconnected/auth/kubeconfig

# Get the ingress CA certificate
INGRESS_CA=$(oc get secret -n openshift-ingress-operator router-ca -o jsonpath="{.data.tls\.crt}" | base64 -d)

# Create ConfigMap with ingress CA
cat << EOF | oc apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: user-ca-bundle
  namespace: openshift-config
data:
  ca-bundle.crt: |
$(echo "$INGRESS_CA" | sed 's/^/    /')
EOF

docs.title: Step 3: Configure Proxy to Trust CA
docs.text:
# Patch proxy configuration to use the CA bundle
oc patch proxy/cluster --type=merge \
  -p '{"spec":{"trustedCA":{"name":"user-ca-bundle"}}}'

# Verify
oc get proxy/cluster -o jsonpath='{.spec.trustedCA}'
# Output: {"name":"user-ca-bundle"}

Note: This will cause several cluster operators to restart (ingress, monitoring, authentication, etc.). Wait 2-3 minutes for stabilization.

docs.title: Step 4: Verify Available Upgrades
docs.text:
# Wait for operators to stabilize
watch 'oc get co | grep -vE "True.*False.*False"'

# Check available upgrades
oc adm upgrade

Expected Output:

Cluster version is 4.18.14

Recommended updates:

  VERSION     IMAGE
  4.18.16     mirror-registry.example.local:8443/ocp4/openshift/release-images@sha256:...
  4.18.15     mirror-registry.example.local:8443/ocp4/openshift/release-images@sha256:...

docs.title: Step 5: Trigger Upgrade
docs.text:
# Upgrade to 4.18.15
oc adm upgrade --to=4.18.15

# Monitor progress
watch 'oc get clusterversion; echo ""; oc get co | grep -vE "True.*False.*False"'

docs.title: Step 6: Monitor Upgrade Progress
docs.text:
# Watch ClusterVersion
oc get clusterversion -w

# Check operator status during upgrade
oc get co

# View upgrade events
oc get events -n openshift-cluster-version --sort-by='.lastTimestamp'

docs.title: Upgrade Timeline (Typical for SNO)
docs.text:
Phase Duration What Happens Preparation 1-2 min Pulls new release image, validates Control Plane 10-15 min Updates kube-apiserver, etcd, controllers Operators 15-20 min Updates all cluster operators Node 5-10 min Node drain/reboot (SNO: brief API unavailability) Finalization 2-3 min Final reconciliation

Total: ~30-45 minutes for SNO

docs.title: Verification After Upgrade
docs.text:
# Check version
oc get clusterversion
# Should show: VERSION 4.18.15, PROGRESSING False

# Verify all operators healthy
oc get co | grep -vE "True.*False.*False"
# Should show only header (all healthy)

# Check nodes
oc get nodes
# Should show: Ready, version 4.18.15

Method 1: Red Hat Ecosystem Catalog (Recommended)

Browse: https://catalog.redhat.com/software/operators/

  2. Click on the operator

# BEST: Get complete channel/version info as JSON

  .status | 
  {defaultChannel, channels: [.channels[] | {name, currentCSV}]}'

Example JSON output:

  "channels": [

docs.title: Phase 27: True Network Isolation (December 2025)
docs.text: Date: December 12, 2025

docs.title: Problem: Previous Setup Was Not Truly Disconnected
docs.text:
The previous SNO cluster had internet access because: 1. The sno-test libvirt network was created with nat mode (default) 2. Default Red Hat catalog sources (redhat-operators, etc.) were still active 3. Operators could be installed from public internet

Evidence: From inside the SNO VM: 

curl -s --connect-timeout 5 https://google.com -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}"
# Output: 200  <-- Should have been timeout/failure!

docs.title: Step 1: Delete Old SNO and Network
docs.text:
# Stop mirror-registry to detach from network
kcli stop vm mirror-registry

# Delete SNO VM
kcli delete vm sno-disconnected -y

# Detach network interface from mirror-registry
sudo virsh detach-interface mirror-registry network --mac 52:54:00:16:44:5c --config

# Delete old network
kcli delete network sno-test -y

docs.title: Step 2: Create Isolated Network
docs.text:
# Create network with --isolated flag (NO NAT, NO INTERNET)
kcli create network -c 198.51.100.0/24 --domain example.local --isolated sno-test

# Verify network mode
sudo virsh net-dumpxml sno-test | grep forward
# Should return NOTHING (no <forward> element = isolated)

# Alternative verification
kcli list network | grep sno-test
# Should show: sno-test | routed | 198.51.100.0/24 | ... | isolated

docs.title: Step 3: Add DNS Entries
docs.text:
# Add mirror-registry DNS
sudo virsh net-update sno-test add dns-host \
  "<host ip=\"198.51.100.141\">
    <hostname>mirror-registry.example.local</hostname>
    <hostname>mirror-registry</hostname>
  </host>" --live --config

# Add SNO DNS entries
sudo virsh net-update sno-test add dns-host \
  "<host ip=\"198.51.100.60\">
    <hostname>sno-disconnected.example.local</hostname>
    <hostname>api.sno-disconnected.example.local</hostname>
    <hostname>api-int.sno-disconnected.example.local</hostname>
  </host>" --live --config

docs.title: Step 4: Reattach Mirror Registry to Network
docs.text:
# Attach with same MAC address (keeps same IP via DHCP)
sudo virsh attach-interface mirror-registry network sno-test \
  --model virtio --mac 52:54:00:16:44:5c --config

# Start mirror-registry
kcli start vm mirror-registry

# Wait for services
sleep 60

# Verify registry works (from homelab-server)
curl -sk https://mirror-registry.example.local:8443/v2/
# Expected: true

docs.title: Step 5: Verify Isolation
docs.text:
# From mirror-registry VM (should FAIL):
kcli ssh mirror-registry "curl -s --connect-timeout 5 https://google.com -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}'"
# Expected: 000 (timeout/connection refused)

# From mirror-registry VM (should WORK):
kcli ssh mirror-registry "getent hosts sno-disconnected.example.local"
# Expected: 198.51.100.60 sno-disconnected.example.local

docs.title: Step 6: Generate New Agent ISO
docs.text:
# Clean old install directory
rm -rf ~/sno-disconnected
mkdir -p ~/sno-disconnected
cd ~/sno-disconnected

# Create install-config.yaml (see Phase 10)
# Create agent-config.yaml (see Phase 10)

# Generate ISO
openshift-install agent create image --dir=. --log-level=info

# Copy to libvirt
sudo cp agent.x86_64.iso /var/lib/libvirt/images/sno-agent.iso

docs.title: Step 7: Create and Boot SNO VM
docs.text:
kcli create vm \
  -P numcpus=8 \
  -P memory=16384 \
  -P disks=[120] \
  -P nets="[{\"name\":\"sno-test\",\"mac\":\"52:54:00:aa:bb:60\"}]" \
  -P iso=/var/lib/libvirt/images/sno-agent.iso \
  -P start=false \
  sno-disconnected

docs.title: Step 4: Install Cincinnati Operator (OSUS)
docs.text:
# Create namespace
oc create namespace openshift-update-service

# Create OperatorGroup
cat << EOF | oc apply -f -
apiVersion: operators.coreos.com/v1
kind: OperatorGroup
metadata:
  name: update-service-operator-group
  namespace: openshift-update-service
spec:
  targetNamespaces:
    - openshift-update-service
EOF

# Create Subscription
cat << EOF | oc apply -f -
apiVersion: operators.coreos.com/v1alpha1
kind: Subscription
metadata:
  name: cincinnati-operator
  namespace: openshift-update-service
spec:
  channel: v1
  installPlanApproval: Automatic
  name: cincinnati-operator
  source: cs-redhat-operator-index-v4-18
  sourceNamespace: openshift-marketplace
EOF

# Wait for CSV to succeed
sleep 60
oc get csv -n openshift-update-service
# Should show: update-service-operator.v5.0.3 Succeeded

docs.title: Step 5: Configure CA Trust for Mirror Registry
docs.text:
# Read the mirror-registry CA
MIRROR_CA=$(cat ~/oc-mirror-workspace/mirror-registry-ca.pem)

# Create ConfigMap with CA (using heredoc that expands variables)
cat << EOF | oc apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: mirror-registry-ca
  namespace: openshift-config
data:
  updateservice-registry: |
$(cat ~/oc-mirror-workspace/mirror-registry-ca.pem | sed 's/^/    /')
EOF

# Patch image config to trust the registry
oc patch image.config.openshift.io/cluster --type=merge \
  -p '{"spec":{"additionalTrustedCA":{"name":"mirror-registry-ca"}}}'

Note: The heredoc with EOF (not 'EOF') allows variable/command expansion.

docs.title: Step 6: Deploy UpdateService CR
docs.text:
cat << EOF | oc apply -f -
apiVersion: updateservice.operator.openshift.io/v1
kind: UpdateService
metadata:
  name: update-service-oc-mirror
  namespace: openshift-update-service
spec:
  graphDataImage: mirror-registry.example.local:8443/ocp4/openshift/graph-image:latest
  releases: mirror-registry.example.local:8443/ocp4/openshift/release-images
  replicas: 1
EOF

# Wait for pods
sleep 60
oc get pods -n openshift-update-service

docs.title: Step 7: Create OSUS Route and Configure Cluster
docs.text:
# Create route for OSUS
oc create route edge update-service-oc-mirror-route \
  --service=update-service-oc-mirror-policy-engine \
  --namespace=openshift-update-service

# Get route URL
OSUS_ROUTE=$(oc get route -n openshift-update-service update-service-oc-mirror-route \
  -o jsonpath='{.spec.host}')
echo "OSUS Route: ${OSUS_ROUTE}"

# Get ingress CA
INGRESS_CA=$(oc get secret -n openshift-ingress-operator router-ca \
  -o jsonpath='{.data.tls\.crt}' | base64 -d)

# Read mirror CA
MIRROR_CA=$(cat ~/oc-mirror-workspace/mirror-registry-ca.pem)

# Create user-ca-bundle with both CAs (combine into single bundle)
cat << EOF | oc apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: user-ca-bundle
  namespace: openshift-config
data:
  ca-bundle.crt: |
$(echo "$MIRROR_CA" | sed 's/^/    /')
$(echo "$INGRESS_CA" | sed 's/^/    /')
EOF

# Configure proxy to trust CAs
oc patch proxy/cluster --type=merge \
  -p '{"spec":{"trustedCA":{"name":"user-ca-bundle"}}}'

# Configure ClusterVersion to use OSUS
oc patch clusterversion version --type merge \
  -p "{\"spec\":{\"upstream\":\"https://${OSUS_ROUTE}/api/upgrades_info/v1/graph\",\"channel\":\"stable-4.18\"}}"

docs.text:

oc adm upgrade

# Expected output shows:
# Upstream: https://update-service-oc-mirror-route-openshift-update-service.apps.sno-disconnected.example.local/api/upgrades_info/v1/graph
# Channel: stable-4.18 (available channels: ...)
#
# Recommended updates:
#   VERSION     IMAGE
#   4.18.16     mirror-registry.example.local:8443/ocp4/openshift/release-images@sha256:...
#   4.18.15     mirror-registry.example.local:8443/ocp4/openshift/release-images@sha256:...

docs.title: Step 9: Add Disconnected Cluster Banner (Best Practice)
docs.text:
Add a visible warning banner to the OpenShift console so users know this is a disconnected environment:

# Apply the console notification
oc apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: console.openshift.io/v1
kind: ConsoleNotification
metadata:
  name: disconnected-cluster-banner
spec:
  text: "⚠️ DISCONNECTED CLUSTER - This cluster has no internet access. All images are served from the local mirror registry."
  location: BannerTop
  color: '#fff'
  backgroundColor: '#c9190b'
  link:
    href: 'https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.18/installing/disconnected_install/index.html'
    text: 'Disconnected Install Docs'
EOF

# Verify
oc get consolenotification disconnected-cluster-banner

The manifest is also available at manifests/console-notification-disconnected.yaml.

Result: A red banner appears at the top of the OpenShift console on every page.

docs.title: Step 10: Disable Remote Health Reporting (Recommended)
docs.text:
In disconnected environments, the Insights Operator shows persistent errors because it cannot reach Red Hat Insights:

Unable to report: unable to build request to connect to Insights server

To disable these errors, remove the cloud.openshift.com entry from the global pull secret.

Reference: OCP 4.18 - Opting out of remote health reporting

export KUBECONFIG=~/sno-disconnected/auth/kubeconfig

# Extract the global pull secret
oc extract secret/pull-secret -n openshift-config --to=/tmp --confirm

# Verify cloud.openshift.com is present
cat /tmp/.dockerconfigjson | jq '.auths | keys'

# Remove the cloud.openshift.com entry
cat /tmp/.dockerconfigjson | jq 'del(.auths["cloud.openshift.com"])' > /tmp/.dockerconfigjson.new
mv /tmp/.dockerconfigjson.new /tmp/.dockerconfigjson

# Verify cloud.openshift.com is removed
cat /tmp/.dockerconfigjson | jq '.auths | keys'

# Update the cluster secret
oc set data secret/pull-secret -n openshift-config --from-file=.dockerconfigjson=/tmp/.dockerconfigjson

# Clean up
rm /tmp/.dockerconfigjson

# Wait for changes to propagate (1-2 minutes)
sleep 60

# Verify Insights operator is no longer degraded
oc get co insights
# Expected: AVAILABLE=True, DEGRADED=False

Result: The Insights Operator will stop attempting to connect to Red Hat and show AVAILABLE=True, DEGRADED=False.

Note: This disables both Telemetry and Insights Operator. This is expected for truly disconnected clusters.

docs.title: Phase 29: Upgrade to OCP 4.19 (Minor Version Upgrade)
docs.text: This phase documents upgrading from OCP 4.18.x to 4.19.x in a disconnected environment.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Cluster running OCP 4.18.x (e.g., 4.18.14)
  • OSUS (Cincinnati) configured and working
  • Access to homelab-server (jumphost with internet)

docs.title: Available 4.19 Versions (stable-4.19 channel)
docs.text:
Check latest versions: 

cd ~/oc-mirror-workspace
export REGISTRY_AUTH_FILE=./pull-secret.json
oc-mirror list releases --channel=stable-4.19 2>&1 | grep "^4\.19" | tail -10

As of December 2025: | Version | Status | |---------|--------| | 4.19.0 | First GA | | 4.19.19 - 4.19.21 | Latest stable |

docs.title: Step 1: Update ImageSetConfiguration for 4.19
docs.text:
Edit imageset-config.yaml on homelab-server:

cd ~/oc-mirror-workspace
vi imageset-config.yaml

Update both the platform channel AND the operator catalog to 4.19:

Pattern for future upgrades: When upgrading to 4.20, 4.21, etc., repeat this pattern: - Add new stable-4.XX channel - Change operator catalog from v4.YY to v4.XX

apiVersion: mirror.openshift.io/v2alpha1
kind: ImageSetConfiguration
mirror:
  platform:
    architectures:
      - amd64
    channels:
      - name: stable-4.18
        minVersion: '4.18.14'
        maxVersion: '4.18.21'
      - name: stable-4.19                    # <-- ADD new version channel
        minVersion: '4.19.19'
        maxVersion: '4.19.21'
    graph: true

  operators:
    - catalog: registry.redhat.io/redhat/redhat-operator-index:v4.19  # <-- CHANGE from v4.18 to v4.19
      packages:
        - name: cincinnati-operator
          channels:
            - name: v1
              minVersion: '5.0.3'
              maxVersion: '5.0.3'
        - name: local-storage-operator
          channels:
            - name: stable
        - name: cluster-observability-operator
          channels:
            - name: stable
        - name: submariner
          channels:
            - name: stable-0.19
        - name: cluster-logging
          channels:
            - name: stable-6.1
        - name: elasticsearch-operator
          channels:
            - name: stable-5.8
        - name: openshift-gitops-operator
          channels:
            - name: latest

Key changes: 1. Added stable-4.19 channel under platform 2. Changed operator catalog from v4.18 → v4.19

docs.title: Step 2: Mirror OCP Release Images and Operators
docs.text:
cd ~/oc-mirror-workspace

# IMPORTANT: Unset this env var (known oc-mirror v2 bug with REGISTRY_AUTH_FILE)
unset REGISTRY_AUTH_FILE

# Run oc-mirror v2 - TESTED WORKING COMMAND
oc-mirror -c ./imageset-config.yaml \
  --workspace file://$(pwd)/workspace \
  docker://mirror-registry.example.local:8443/ocp4 \
  --authfile $(pwd)/pull-secret.json \
  --v2 2>&1 | tee oc-mirror.log

# Expected output:
# - New release images for the configured OCP versions
# - Operator images from the configured catalog version
# - Updated graph data with upgrade paths
# - New CatalogSource manifest for operators

Note: This mirrors both OCP release images AND operators in a single command.

docs.title: ⚠️ oc-mirror v2 Command Reference (TESTED)
docs.text:
Working command template: 

oc-mirror -c ./imageset-config.yaml \
  --workspace file://$(pwd)/workspace \
  docker://<registry>:<port>/<namespace> \
  --authfile $(pwd)/pull-secret.json \
  --v2

Required flags: | Flag | Description | |------|-------------| | -c <file> | Path to imageset-config.yaml | | --workspace file://<path> | Local workspace directory (MUST come before docker://) | | docker://<dest> | Destination registry | | --authfile <path> | Path to pull-secret.json (REQUIRED for auth) | | --v2 | Use oc-mirror v2 engine (MUST be at end) |

Flags that DO NOT EXIST in v2: | Invalid Flag | Notes | |--------------|-------| | --continue-on-error | ❌ Does not exist | | --rebuild-catalogs | ❌ Does not exist | | --config | ❌ Use -c instead |

Common errors: | Error | Solution | |-------|----------| | unauthorized: access to the requested resource is not authorized | Add --authfile $(pwd)/pull-secret.json | | unknown flag: --continue-on-error | Remove the flag - it doesn't exist | | parsing environment variable REGISTRY_AUTH_FILE | Run unset REGISTRY_AUTH_FILE first |

docs.title: Step 3: Apply Updated Cluster Resources
docs.text:
export KUBECONFIG=~/sno-disconnected/auth/kubeconfig

# Apply new IDMS, CatalogSource, and other resources
oc apply -f ./workspace/working-dir/cluster-resources/

# Expected: New CatalogSource for v4.19 operators
# cs-redhat-operator-index-v4-19 created

# Verify new CatalogSource is ready
oc get catalogsource -n openshift-marketplace
# Should show: cs-redhat-operator-index-v4-19

# Verify operators available from v4.19 catalog
oc get packagemanifest -n openshift-marketplace

# Restart OSUS to pick up new graph data
oc delete pod -n openshift-update-service -l app=update-service-oc-mirror

# Wait for OSUS pod to be ready
sleep 60
oc get pods -n openshift-update-service

Note: The old v4.18 CatalogSource will remain but can be deleted after successful upgrade.

docs.title: Step 4: Acknowledge Kubernetes 1.32 API Removals
docs.text:
OCP 4.19 uses Kubernetes 1.32 which removes deprecated APIs. You must acknowledge this:

# Check if admin-acks configmap exists
oc get configmap admin-acks -n openshift-config

# If it exists, patch it:
oc -n openshift-config patch cm admin-acks --type=merge \
  -p '{"data":{"ack-4.18-kube-1.32-api-removals-in-4.19":"true"}}'

# If it doesn't exist, create it:
oc create configmap admin-acks -n openshift-config \
  --from-literal=ack-4.18-kube-1.32-api-removals-in-4.19=true

# Verify
oc get configmap admin-acks -n openshift-config -o yaml

Reference: Red Hat KB Article 7112216

docs.title: Step 5: Handle Insights Operator (Disconnected Workaround)
docs.text:
The insights operator is always degraded in disconnected environments. Allow upgrade despite this:

# Allow upgrade with degraded operators
oc annotate clusterversion version \
  "unsupported.operator.openshift.io/allow-upgrade=true" --overwrite

# Verify annotation
oc get clusterversion version -o jsonpath='{.metadata.annotations}' | jq .

docs.title: Step 6: Switch to stable-4.19 Channel
docs.text:
# Switch channel
oc adm upgrade channel stable-4.19

# Verify channel change
oc get clusterversion version -o jsonpath='{.spec.channel}'
# Expected: stable-4.19

# Check available upgrades
oc adm upgrade
# Should now show 4.19.x versions from mirror

docs.title: Step 7: Trigger Upgrade to 4.19
docs.text:
# Check what's available
oc adm upgrade

# Start upgrade to 4.19.21 (or latest available)
oc adm upgrade --to=4.19.21 --force

# Monitor upgrade progress (45-60 min for SNO)
watch -n 30 'echo "=== ClusterVersion ==="; oc get clusterversion; echo ""; echo "=== Nodes ==="; oc get nodes; echo ""; echo "=== Degraded Operators ==="; oc get co | grep -v "True.*False.*False"'

docs.title: Step 8: Post-Upgrade Verification
docs.text:
# Verify final version
oc get clusterversion
# Expected: VERSION = 4.19.21

# Check all nodes ready
oc get nodes
# Expected: Ready, v1.32.x

# Check all cluster operators
oc get co
# All should be Available=True, Degraded=False (except insights)

# Check pods
oc get pods -A | grep -v Running | grep -v Completed

# Verify console accessible
oc whoami --show-console
