docs.title: Quick Reference - All Commands (Copy/Paste)
docs.text:
Complete upgrade commands in one block for easy execution:

# ============================================================================
# PHASE 29: UPGRADE 4.18 → 4.19 - QUICK REFERENCE
# ============================================================================
# Run these commands on homelab-server

# --- STEP 1: Edit imageset-config.yaml ---
cd ~/oc-mirror-workspace
# Add stable-4.19 channel and change operator catalog to v4.19
vi imageset-config.yaml

# --- STEP 2: Mirror 4.19 images + operators (1-2 hours) ---
export REGISTRY_AUTH_FILE=./pull-secret.json
oc mirror --v2 \
  --config imageset-config.yaml \
  docker://mirror-registry.example.local:8443/ocp4 \
  --workspace file://./workspace \
  --authfile pull-secret.json

# --- STEP 3: Apply cluster resources ---
export KUBECONFIG=~/sno-disconnected/auth/kubeconfig
oc apply -f ./workspace/working-dir/cluster-resources/
oc get catalogsource -n openshift-marketplace
oc delete pod -n openshift-update-service -l app=update-service-oc-mirror
sleep 60 && oc get pods -n openshift-update-service

# --- STEP 4: Acknowledge API removal ---
oc -n openshift-config patch cm admin-acks --type=merge \
  -p '{"data":{"ack-4.18-kube-1.32-api-removals-in-4.19":"true"}}' 2>/dev/null || \
oc create configmap admin-acks -n openshift-config \
  --from-literal=ack-4.18-kube-1.32-api-removals-in-4.19=true

# --- STEP 5: Allow upgrade with degraded insights ---
oc annotate clusterversion version \
  "unsupported.operator.openshift.io/allow-upgrade=true" --overwrite

# --- STEP 6: Switch channel ---
oc adm upgrade channel stable-4.19
oc get clusterversion version -o jsonpath='{.spec.channel}' && echo ""

# --- STEP 7: Trigger upgrade (45-60 min) ---
oc adm upgrade
oc adm upgrade --to=4.19.21 --force

# --- STEP 8: Monitor upgrade ---
watch -n 30 'oc get clusterversion; echo "---"; oc get nodes; echo "---"; oc get co | grep -v "True.*False.*False"'

# --- STEP 9: Verify ---
oc get clusterversion
oc get nodes
oc get co

# --- STEP 10: Cleanup old operator catalog ---
# After successful upgrade, remove the old version's catalog
oc get catalogsource -n openshift-marketplace
# Delete the old v4.18 catalog (no longer needed on 4.19 cluster)
oc delete catalogsource cs-redhat-operator-index-v4-18 -n openshift-marketplace
# Verify only v4.19 catalog remains
oc get catalogsource -n openshift-marketplace

Note: After a minor version upgrade, you'll have both the old and new operator catalogs. Always delete the old catalog to: - Prevent installing incompatible operator versions - Keep the OperatorHub clean - Avoid confusion in the web console

docs.title: Mirror Registry Memory Issues (oc-mirror hangs/fails)
docs.text:
Symptoms: - oc-mirror hangs or crashes during operator mirroring - kswapd0 process using high CPU on mirror-registry VM - Registry API returns empty or errors

Cause: Mirror-registry VM has insufficient RAM for large mirror operations.

Diagnosis: 

# Check if VM is swapping heavily
kcli ssh mirror-registry "top -bn1 | head -10"

# Look for kswapd0 using high CPU = memory pressure

Solution - Increase VM RAM: 

# Stop VM
kcli stop vm mirror-registry

# Increase RAM (6GB recommended minimum, 8GB for large mirrors)
kcli update vm mirror-registry -P memory=6144

# Start VM
kcli start vm mirror-registry

# Wait for registry to start (~30 seconds)
sleep 30
curl -sk https://mirror-registry.example.local:8443/v2/

Recommended RAM by mirror size:

Mirror Content Minimum RAM OCP only (3 versions) 4 GB OCP + few operators 6 GB OCP + many operators 8 GB Large enterprise mirror 12+ GB

docs.title: oc-mirror Channel Errors
docs.text:
Symptom: 

invalid default channel configuration for package "X": the default channel "Y" was filtered out

Cause: You specified a channel that's not the default, and oc-mirror requires the default channel to be included.

Solution: Use the correct default channel. Find it with:

oc get packagemanifest <operator-name> -o jsonpath='{.status.defaultChannel}'

# Or check Red Hat Catalog: https://catalog.redhat.com/software/operators/

docs.text:

StatusCode: 413, "<html><head><title>413 Request Entity Too Large</title></head>..."
[Worker] error mirroring image ... uploading layer chunked: StatusCode: 413

docs.title: Technical Explanation
docs.text:
Quay Architecture:

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    Quay Container (quay-app)                │
│                                                             │
│   ┌──────────┐    ┌─────────────────┐    ┌──────────────┐  │
│   │  nginx   │───►│  gunicorn-web   │    │  PostgreSQL  │  │
│   │  :8443   │    │  (API/UI)       │    │  (metadata)  │  │
│   │          │───►│                 │    └──────────────┘  │
│   │          │    │ gunicorn-       │    ┌──────────────┐  │
│   │          │───►│ registry        │───►│  /datastorage│  │
│   │          │    │ (blob uploads)  │    │  (images)    │  │
│   └──────────┘    └─────────────────┘    └──────────────┘  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

The Problem:

  1. nginx sits in front of all Quay endpoints
  2. nginx has client_max_body_size limits in /conf/nginx/nginx.conf
  3. Default limit: 5MB for general requests
  4. OCP image layers can be 100MB - 500MB+ each
  5. When oc-mirror uploads a layer > 5MB, nginx rejects it with HTTP 413

nginx Config Locations:

/conf/nginx/nginx.conf           → client_max_body_size 5M;    (global default)
/conf/nginx/server-base.conf     → client_max_body_size 5M;    (general endpoints)
                                 → client_max_body_size 20G;   (blob upload endpoints)

The Issue:

The server-base.conf has 20GB limits for blob endpoints, but only if MAXIMUM_LAYER_SIZE is set in Quay's config. Without this setting, the config template uses the 5MB default.

Config Template Logic:

# /conf/nginx/server-base.conf.jnj (Jinja2 template)
location /v2/ {
    client_max_body_size {{ maximum_layer_size }};  # Uses MAXIMUM_LAYER_SIZE from config
}

If MAXIMUM_LAYER_SIZE is not set → defaults to 5MB → 413 errors.

docs.title: Solution
docs.text:
# SSH to mirror-registry
kcli ssh mirror-registry

# Add MAXIMUM_LAYER_SIZE to Quay config
echo "MAXIMUM_LAYER_SIZE: 20G" | sudo tee -a /opt/quay/quay-config/config.yaml

# Restart Quay containers to regenerate nginx config
sudo podman restart quay-app quay-postgres quay-redis

# Wait for startup (~30-60 seconds)
sleep 60

# Verify registry is working
curl -sk https://localhost:8443/v2/_catalog

# Verify nginx config was updated
sudo podman exec quay-app grep "client_max_body_size" /conf/nginx/server-base.conf
# Should show: client_max_body_size 20G;

exit

docs.title: Why This Happens with OCP Images
docs.text:
Image Type Typical Layer Size Affected by 5MB limit? Alpine/busybox 2-5 MB No Standard app 10-50 MB Yes OCP component 50-200 MB Yes OCP release payload 100-500 MB Yes

OCP releases contain large base images (RHEL UBI, Go binaries, etc.) that easily exceed 5MB.

docs.title: Prevention
docs.text:
Add MAXIMUM_LAYER_SIZE: 20G during initial mirror-registry installation (see Phase 3).

Recommended Quay config additions for OCP mirroring:

# /opt/quay/quay-config/config.yaml
MAXIMUM_LAYER_SIZE: 20G           # Allow large OCP image layers
FEATURE_PROXY_STORAGE: true       # Enable storage proxy (optional)
CREATE_NAMESPACE_ON_PUSH: true    # Auto-create namespaces (already default)

docs.title: OLM Cluster Operator Unavailable (CreateContainerError)
docs.text:
Symptoms: - oc get co olm shows Available=False, Progressing=True - Message: OperatorcontrollerDeploymentOperatorControllerControllerManagerAvailable: Waiting for Deployment - Pod in CreateContainerError state with many restarts

oc get pods -n openshift-operator-controller
# NAME                                                 READY   STATUS               RESTARTS
# operator-controller-controller-manager-xxx-yyy       0/2     CreateContainerError 29+

Diagnosis: 

# Check pod events
oc describe pod -n openshift-operator-controller $(oc get pods -n openshift-operator-controller -o name | head -1) | tail -30

Look for these error patterns: - Error: context deadline exceeded - kubelet may be retrying requests that are timing out in CRI-O due to system load - Container name reservation conflicts

Cause: CRI-O has stale container state with orphaned name reservations blocking new container creation. This happens when previous container creations timed out but left orphaned state.

Solution: 

# Delete the stuck pod to force fresh container creation
oc delete pod -n openshift-operator-controller $(oc get pods -n openshift-operator-controller -o name | head -1)

# Wait for new pod
sleep 10

# Verify pod is running
oc get pods -n openshift-operator-controller

# Verify OLM operator is healthy
oc get co olm

docs.title: Understanding Shared Image Layers
docs.text:
OpenShift releases use content-addressable storage with SHA256 digests. This means:

4.18.14 ──┐
4.18.30 ──┼──> etcd:sha256:abc123, kube-apiserver:sha256:def456, ...
4.19.20 ──┤    (same underlying images shared across versions!)
4.19.21 ──┘

Key insight: Minor versions (4.18 → 4.19) share ~80-90% of container images because: - Most Kubernetes components remain the same - Only version-specific components differ - Blobs are deduplicated by SHA256 digest

docs.title: Expected Storage Usage
docs.text: Content Approximate Size 1 OCP version 50-70 GB 2 OCP versions (4.18 + 4.19) 80-100 GB (shared layers) 3 OCP versions 100-120 GB + Operators (5-10) +20-40 GB

docs.title: Cleanup Reality
docs.text:
When you "delete" old version tags:

Action What Happens Space Freed Delete 4.18.x tags Tag references removed Minimal Keep 4.19.x only Shared blobs still needed ~5-10% Delete ALL old versions Orphan blobs can be GC'd Variable

Why? Deleting a tag doesn't delete the underlying blobs if ANY other tag references them.

docs.title: Using the Prune Script
docs.text:
cd ~/oc-mirror-workspace

# Check current disk usage
./prune-mirror-registry.sh --check

# Preview what would be deleted (safe)
./prune-mirror-registry.sh --dry-run

# Execute deletion (after review)
./prune-mirror-registry.sh --execute

# Run garbage collection
./prune-mirror-registry.sh --gc

docs.title: Quay-Based Mirror Registry Notes
docs.text:
The mirror-registry installer uses Red Hat Quay as the backend, which has specific GC behavior:

  1. Tag deletion removes API-level references
  2. Manifest GC marks orphaned manifests (runs automatically)
  3. Blob GC deletes unused blobs (runs periodically)

For Quay registries, expect: - GC happens automatically over 24-48 hours - Immediate space reclamation requires database-level cleanup (not recommended) - Disk usage may not decrease immediately after tag deletion

docs.title: Best Practice: Minimal Mirroring
docs.text:
To minimize storage:

# imageset-config.yaml - Keep only what you need
mirror:
  platform:
    channels:
      - name: stable-4.19
        minVersion: '4.19.20'   # Only latest patch
        maxVersion: '4.19.21'
        # Don't include old 4.18 channel after upgrade

After upgrading to 4.19: 1. Remove 4.18 channel from imageset-config.yaml 2. Delete old operator catalog: oc delete catalogsource cs-redhat-operator-index-v4-18 -n openshift-marketplace 3. Run prune script (tags only - blobs will GC over time)

docs.title: Quay Auto-Prune Configuration
docs.text:
The mirror-registry uses Red Hat Quay which supports automatic pruning of old tags.

Enable auto-prune (already added during Phase 3 setup):

# On mirror-registry VM
sudo tee -a /opt/quay/quay-config/config.yaml << 'EOF'

# Enable automatic pruning of old tags
FEATURE_AUTO_PRUNE: true
EOF

sudo podman restart quay-app

Check Quay garbage collection status:

kcli ssh mirror-registry "sudo podman logs quay-app 2>&1 | grep -i -E '(garbage|gc|prune)' | tail -20"

Important Quay GC behavior: - Blob GC runs automatically in background (24-48 hour cycle) - Deleting manifests doesn't immediately free space - Shared blobs remain until ALL references are deleted - FEATURE_AUTO_PRUNE removes old tags automatically based on policies

docs.title: Phase 30: Upgrade to OCP 4.20 (4.19 → 4.20)
docs.text:
Date: December 18, 2025

This phase documents upgrading from OCP 4.19.21 to 4.20.8 in a disconnected environment.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Cluster running OCP 4.19.x (e.g., 4.19.21)
  • OSUS (Cincinnati) configured and working
  • Mirror registry with sufficient space (200GB recommended)

docs.title: Available 4.20 Versions (stable-4.20 channel)
docs.text:
Check latest versions: 

cd ~/oc-mirror-workspace
oc-mirror list releases --channel=stable-4.20 2>&1 | grep "^4\.20" | tail -10

As of December 2025: | Version | Status | |---------|--------| | 4.20.0 | First GA | | 4.20.7 - 4.20.8 | Latest stable |

docs.title: Step 1: Update ImageSetConfiguration for 4.20
docs.text:
Edit imageset-config.yaml on homelab-server:

cd ~/oc-mirror-workspace
vi imageset-config.yaml

Add 4.20 channel AND update operator catalog to v4.20:

apiVersion: mirror.openshift.io/v2alpha1
kind: ImageSetConfiguration
mirror:
  platform:
    architectures:
      - amd64
    channels:
      - name: stable-4.19
        minVersion: '4.19.20'
        maxVersion: '4.19.21'
      - name: stable-4.20                    # <-- ADD new version channel
        minVersion: '4.20.7'
        maxVersion: '4.20.8'
    graph: true

  operators:
    - catalog: registry.redhat.io/redhat/redhat-operator-index:v4.20  # <-- CHANGE from v4.19 to v4.20
      packages:
        - name: cincinnati-operator
          channels:
            - name: v1
        - name: local-storage-operator
          channels:
            - name: stable
        # ... other operators ...

Also run the version update script:

./update-imageset-versions.sh --update

docs.title: Step 2: Mirror OCP 4.20 Release Images and Operators
docs.text:
cd ~/oc-mirror-workspace

# CRITICAL: Unset REGISTRY_AUTH_FILE (known v2 bug)
unset REGISTRY_AUTH_FILE

# Run oc-mirror v2 (1-2 hours)
oc-mirror -c ./imageset-config.yaml \
  --workspace file://$(pwd)/workspace \
  docker://mirror-registry.example.local:8443/ocp4 \
  --authfile $(pwd)/pull-secret.json \
  --v2 2>&1 | tee oc-mirror-4.20.log

Note: If you encounter 413 Request Entity Too Large errors, see the troubleshooting section about MAXIMUM_LAYER_SIZE.

docs.title: Step 3: Apply Updated Cluster Resources
docs.text:
export KUBECONFIG=~/sno-disconnected/auth/kubeconfig

# Apply IDMS/ITMS and new CatalogSource
oc apply -f ./workspace/working-dir/cluster-resources/idms-oc-mirror.yaml
oc apply -f ./workspace/working-dir/cluster-resources/itms-oc-mirror.yaml
oc apply -f ./workspace/working-dir/cluster-resources/cs-redhat-operator-index-v4-20.yaml

# Verify v4.20 CatalogSource is ready
oc get catalogsource -n openshift-marketplace
# Should show: cs-redhat-operator-index-v4-20

# Restart OSUS to pick up new graph data
oc rollout restart deployment/update-service-oc-mirror -n openshift-update-service
oc rollout status deployment/update-service-oc-mirror -n openshift-update-service --timeout=120s

docs.title: Step 4: Switch to stable-4.20 Channel
docs.text:
# Switch channel
oc adm upgrade channel stable-4.20

# Verify channel change
oc get clusterversion version -o jsonpath='{.spec.channel}'
# Expected: stable-4.20

# Check available upgrades
oc adm upgrade

docs.title: Step 5: Trigger Upgrade to 4.20.8
docs.text:
In disconnected environments, the OSUS graph may not have cross-version upgrade edges. Use --to-image with --force:

# Get the release image from mirror
RELEASE_IMAGE=$(oc adm release info mirror-registry.example.local:8443/ocp4/openshift/release-images:4.20.8-x86_64 \
  -o jsonpath='{.image}')

echo "Release image: ${RELEASE_IMAGE}"

# Trigger upgrade with force (bypasses signature verification in disconnected)
oc adm upgrade --to-image="${RELEASE_IMAGE}" --allow-upgrade-with-warnings --force

docs.title: Step 6: Monitor Upgrade Progress
docs.text:
# Watch progress (45-90 min for SNO)
watch -n 30 'echo "=== ClusterVersion ==="; oc get clusterversion; echo ""; echo "=== Nodes ==="; oc get nodes; echo ""; echo "=== Unhealthy Operators ==="; oc get co | grep -v "True.*False.*False"'

Expected progression:

Progress Duration Status 0-25% 5-10 min Control plane operators updating 25-70% 15-25 min Core operators rolling out 70-85% 10-15 min Network, DNS, OLM updating 85-100% 15-30 min MachineConfig, node reboot

API server may be temporarily unavailable during the upgrade (connection refused or timeouts are normal).

docs.title: Step 7: Post-Upgrade Verification
docs.text:
# Verify final version
oc get clusterversion
# Expected: VERSION = 4.20.8, PROGRESSING = False

# Check node version
oc get nodes
# Expected: Ready, v1.33.6 (Kubernetes 1.33 = OCP 4.20)

# Check all cluster operators healthy
oc get co | grep -v "True.*False.*False"
# Should show only header (all healthy)

# Verify OSUS still working
oc adm upgrade

docs.title: Step 8: Cleanup Old Operator Catalog
docs.text:
After successful upgrade, remove the old v4.19 catalog:

# List current catalogs
oc get catalogsource -n openshift-marketplace

# Delete old v4.19 catalog
oc delete catalogsource cs-redhat-operator-index-v4-19 -n openshift-marketplace

# Verify only v4.20 catalog remains
oc get catalogsource -n openshift-marketplace

docs.title: Upgrade Summary
docs.text: Step Command/Action Duration 1 Edit imageset-config.yaml 5 min 2 oc-mirror (4.20 images) 1-2 hours 3 oc apply -f cluster-resources/ 5 min 4 oc adm upgrade channel stable-4.20 1 min 5 oc adm upgrade --to-image=... 1 min 6 Monitor upgrade 45-90 min 7 Verify 5 min 8 Delete old catalog 1 min Total ~2.5-4 hours

docs.title: Console Not Accessible from macOS via Tailscale
docs.text: Symptom: Cannot connect to console-openshift-console.apps.sno-disconnected.example.local from macOS when using Tailscale for connectivity.

docs.title: Step 1: Verify DNS Resolution
docs.text:
# Check if Tailscale MagicDNS can resolve the hostname
nslookup console-openshift-console.apps.sno-disconnected.example.local

# Check /etc/hosts for static entries
grep -i sno /etc/hosts

Why: The .example.local domain is only configured in the libvirt network DNS on homelab-server. macOS won't resolve it unless: - Entry exists in /etc/hosts - A DNS server that knows about .example.local is configured

Expected /etc/hosts entry: 

198.51.100.60 api.sno-disconnected.example.local api-int.sno-disconnected.example.local oauth-openshift.apps.sno-disconnected.example.local console-openshift-console.apps.sno-disconnected.example.local

docs.title: Step 2: Verify Network Connectivity
docs.text:
# Check Tailscale status and connection to homelab-server
tailscale status

# Ping the SNO node directly
ping -c 1 198.51.100.60

Why: Even with correct DNS, traffic must route through Tailscale to homelab-server (192.0.2.107), then to the isolated network (198.51.100.0/24). Tailscale must be advertising the route.

docs.title: Step 3: Test Port Connectivity
docs.text:
# Test HTTPS port (router/ingress)
nc -zv -w 5 198.51.100.60 443

# Test API port (kube-apiserver)
nc -zv -w 5 198.51.100.60 6443

Why: Identifies which layer is failing: - Port 443 = OpenShift Router/Ingress (serves console, routes) - Port 6443 = Kubernetes API server

Port 443 Port 6443 Meaning ❌ ✅ Router is down, API is up ❌ ❌ Node is down or network issue ✅ ✅ Both services running

docs.title: Step 4: Test HTTP Response
docs.text:
# Test console URL with curl
curl -sk --connect-timeout 10 \
  https://console-openshift-console.apps.sno-disconnected.example.local \
  -o /dev/null -w "HTTP: %{http_code}, Time: %{time_total}s\n"

# Test with explicit IP resolution
curl -sk --connect-timeout 10 \
  --resolve "console-openshift-console.apps.sno-disconnected.example.local:443:198.51.100.60" \
  https://console-openshift-console.apps.sno-disconnected.example.local \
  -o /dev/null -w "HTTP: %{http_code}\n"

Why: Distinguishes between DNS issues and actual service failures: - 000 = Connection failed (timeout, refused, network issue) - 200 = Success - 503 = Service unavailable (backend issue)

docs.title: Step 5: Check Cluster Operators (from homelab-server)
docs.text:
# SSH to homelab-server where cluster access is available
ssh lab-user@homelab-server.example.com

# Set kubeconfig
export KUBECONFIG=/home/lab-user/sno-disconnected/auth/kubeconfig

# Check all cluster operators for issues
oc get co | grep -v 'True.*False.*False'

# Specifically check ingress operator
oc get co ingress

Why: Shows which operators are unhealthy. Pattern True False False = healthy. Look for: - AVAILABLE=False = Service not working - PROGRESSING=True = Operator is updating/recovering - DEGRADED=True = Operator has errors

docs.title: Step 6: Check Router Pod Status
docs.text:
# Check router pods
oc get pods -n openshift-ingress

# Check router events
oc get events -n openshift-ingress --sort-by='.lastTimestamp' | tail -20

Why: The router pod serves all .apps.* traffic. Common issues: - 0/1 Running with restarts = Container crashing - Pending = Scheduling issue - ImagePullBackOff = Can't pull image (disconnected issue)

docs.title: Step 7: Check Router Logs via crictl (bypass kubelet cert issues)
docs.text:
# SSH to SNO node directly
ssh core@198.51.100.60

# Find router container
sudo crictl ps -a | grep router

# Get logs from router container
CONTAINER_ID=$(sudo crictl ps -a | grep router | head -1 | awk '{print $1}')
sudo crictl logs $CONTAINER_ID 2>&1 | head -100
sudo crictl logs $CONTAINER_ID 2>&1 | tail -50

Why: Sometimes oc logs fails with certificate errors. Using crictl directly on the node bypasses the kubelet API and reads container logs from the runtime.

docs.title: Step 8: Check OpenShift API Server
docs.text:
# Check openshift-apiserver pods
oc get pods -n openshift-apiserver

# Check openshift-apiserver operator
oc get co openshift-apiserver

# Check Route API service availability
oc get apiservice v1.route.openshift.io

Why: The router depends on the Routes API (routes.route.openshift.io). If the OpenShift API server is unhealthy, the router can't sync routes and HAProxy won't start.

docs.title: Step 9: Check Node Resources
docs.text:
# SSH to SNO node
ssh core@198.51.100.60

# Check memory
free -h

# Check disk space
df -h / /var

# Check CPU load
uptime

# Check for OOM kills
sudo dmesg | grep -i "out of memory" | tail -5

Why: SNO runs all control plane components on a single node. Resource exhaustion causes cascading failures: - High load average (>8 on 8 vCPU) = CPU contention - Low available memory = Risk of OOM kills - Full disk = etcd/kubelet failures

docs.title: 1. Router Can't Sync Routes (401 Unauthorized)
docs.text:
Symptom: 

failed to list *v1.Route: the server is currently unable to handle the request

Cause: OpenShift API server returning 401 errors for aggregated API calls.

Resolution: Usually self-heals. Wait for the openshift-apiserver to stabilize. Check: 

oc get co openshift-apiserver
oc get apiservice v1.route.openshift.io

docs.title: 2. HAProxy Socket Missing
docs.text:
Symptom: 

can't scrape HAProxy: dial unix /var/lib/haproxy/run/haproxy.sock: no such file or directory

Cause: HAProxy process never started because router couldn't sync routes.

Resolution: Fix the underlying Routes API issue. Router will auto-recover.

docs.title: 3. High Node Load
docs.text:
Symptom: Load average consistently >8 on 8 vCPU node.

Cause: Resource contention on SNO. Too many pods or operators competing.

Resolution: - Increase VM resources (vCPU, RAM) - Reduce workloads - Check for runaway pods: oc adm top pods -A --sort-by=cpu | head -20

docs.title: Quick Recovery Commands
docs.text:
# Force router pod restart (last resort)
oc delete pod -n openshift-ingress -l ingresscontroller.operator.openshift.io/deployment-ingresscontroller=default

# Check if cluster is recovering
watch -n5 'oc get co | grep -v "True.*False.*False"'

# Verify console is accessible
curl -sk https://console-openshift-console.apps.sno-disconnected.example.local -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n"

# 1. Clone or copy the repository to homelab-server
cd ~/sno-disconnected/telemetry-sync

# 2. Create configuration
cp config/telemetry-sync.env.template config/telemetry-sync.env

# 3. Edit configuration with your values
vi config/telemetry-sync.env

# 4. Run installer
./scripts/install-systemd.sh

docs.title: Configuration Required
docs.text:
Before running the installer, set these values in config/telemetry-sync.env:

# Cluster ID
CLUSTER_ID="your-cluster-id"

# Cloud token (from pull-secret)
CLOUD_TOKEN="your-token"

# Verify kubeconfig path
KUBECONFIG="${HOME}/sno-disconnected/auth/kubeconfig"

To get CLUSTER_ID: 

oc get clusterversion version -o jsonpath='{.spec.clusterID}'

To get CLOUD_TOKEN: 

oc extract secret/pull-secret -n openshift-config --to=- | jq -r '.auths["cloud.openshift.com"].auth'

docs.title: telemetry-sync.service
docs.text:
[Service]
Type=oneshot
ExecStart=~/sno-disconnected/telemetry-sync/scripts/process-queue.sh
TimeoutStartSec=600    # 10 minutes max

Key features: - Oneshot service (runs to completion) - 10-minute timeout - Logs to journald - Security hardening enabled

docs.title: telemetry-sync.timer
docs.text:
[Timer]
OnCalendar=*-*-* 03:00:00 UTC
Persistent=true
RandomizedDelaySec=900

Key features: - Runs at 03:00 UTC daily - Persistent=true: Runs immediately if missed (system was off) - Random delay up to 15 minutes

docs.title: Timer Management
docs.text:
# Check timer schedule
systemctl --user list-timers

# Check next run time
systemctl --user list-timers telemetry-sync.timer

# Start/stop timer
systemctl --user start telemetry-sync.timer
systemctl --user stop telemetry-sync.timer

# Enable/disable timer
systemctl --user enable telemetry-sync.timer
systemctl --user disable telemetry-sync.timer

docs.title: Service Management
docs.text:
# Manual run
systemctl --user start telemetry-sync.service

# Check status
systemctl --user status telemetry-sync.service

# View logs
journalctl --user -u telemetry-sync.service -f

# View recent logs
journalctl --user -u telemetry-sync.service --since "1 hour ago"

docs.title: Retry Service
docs.text:
# Manual retry of failed uploads
systemctl --user start telemetry-retry.service

# View retry logs
journalctl --user -u telemetry-retry.service -f

docs.title: Uninstallation
docs.text:
./scripts/install-systemd.sh --uninstall

This will: 1. Stop timers 2. Disable timers 3. Remove unit files 4. Reload systemd daemon

docs.title: Timer Not Running
docs.text:
# Check if user lingering is enabled
loginctl show-user $USER | grep Linger
# Should show: Linger=yes

# If not, enable it
sudo loginctl enable-linger $USER

docs.title: Service Fails to Start
docs.text:
# Check logs
journalctl --user -u telemetry-sync.service -e

# Run health check
~/sno-disconnected/telemetry-sync/scripts/health-check.sh

# Test manually
~/sno-disconnected/telemetry-sync/scripts/process-queue.sh

docs.title: Cannot Connect to Cluster
docs.text:
# Verify kubeconfig
export KUBECONFIG=~/sno-disconnected/auth/kubeconfig
oc whoami
oc get nodes

docs.title: Logging
docs.text: Logs are written to: - journald: journalctl --user -u telemetry-sync.service - File logs: ${QUEUE_DIR}/logs/telemetry-sync.log
